  72: /** Increase default stack size (KB) to prevent stack overflow on deep class hierarchies. */
  73: const STACK_KB = 4096;
  74: const STACK_FLAG = `--stack-size=${STACK_KB}`;
  75: 
  76: /** Re-exec the process with an 8GB heap and larger stack if we're currently below that. */
  77: function ensureHeap(): boolean {
  78:   const nodeOpts = process.env.NODE_OPTIONS || '';
  79:   if (nodeOpts.includes('--max-old-space-size')) return false;
  80: 
  81:   const v8Heap = v8.getHeapStatistics().heap_size_limit;
  82:   if (v8Heap >= HEAP_MB * 1024 * 1024 * 0.9) return false;
  83: 
  84:   // --stack-size is a V8 flag not allowed in NODE_OPTIONS on Node 24+,
  85:   // so pass it only as a direct CLI argument, not via the environment.
  86:   const cliFlags = [HEAP_FLAG];
  87:   if (!nodeOpts.includes('--stack-size')) cliFlags.push(STACK_FLAG);
  88: 
  89:   try {
  90:     execFileSync(process.execPath, [...cliFlags, ...process.argv.slice(1)], {
  91:       stdio: 'inherit',
  92:       env: { ...process.env, NODE_OPTIONS: `${nodeOpts} ${HEAP_FLAG}`.trim() },
  93:     });
  94:   } catch (e: any) {
  95:     process.exitCode = e.status ?? 1;
  96:   }
  97:   return true;
  98: }
  99: 
 100: export interface AnalyzeOptions {
 101:   force?: boolean;
 102:   /**
 103:    * Embedding generation toggle. Commander parses `--embeddings [limit]` as:
 104:    *   - `undefined` when the flag is omitted
 105:    *   - `true` when passed without an argument (use default 50K node cap)
 106:    *   - a string when passed with an argument (`--embeddings 0` disables the
 107:    *     cap, `--embeddings <n>` uses `<n>` as the cap)
 108:    */
 109:   embeddings?: boolean | string;
 110:   /**
 111:    * Explicitly drop existing embeddings on rebuild instead of preserving
 112:    * them. Without this flag, a routine `analyze` keeps any embeddings
 113:    * already present in the index even when `--embeddings` is omitted.
 114:    */
 115:   dropEmbeddings?: boolean;
 116:   skills?: boolean;
 117:   verbose?: boolean;
 118:   /** Skip AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md gitnexus block updates. */
 119:   skipAgentsMd?: boolean;
 120:   /** Omit volatile symbol/relationship counts from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md. */

 121:   noStats?: boolean;
 122:   /** Index the folder even when no .git directory is present. */
 123:   skipGit?: boolean;
 124:   /**
 125:    * Override the default basename-derived registry `name` with a
 126:    * user-supplied alias (#829). Disambiguates repos whose paths share a
 127:    * basename. Persisted — subsequent re-analyses of the same path without
 128:    * `--name` preserve the alias.
 129:    */
 130:   name?: string;
 131:   /**
 132:    * Allow registration even when another path already uses the same
 133:    * `--name` alias (#829). Intentionally a distinct flag from `--force`
 134:    * because the user may want to coexist under the same name WITHOUT
 135:    * paying the cost of a pipeline re-index. Maps to registerRepo's
 136:    * `allowDuplicateName` option end-to-end.
 137:    */
 138:   allowDuplicateName?: boolean;
 139:   /**
 140:    * Override the walker's large-file skip threshold (#991). Value in KB;
 141:    * clamped downstream to the tree-sitter 32 MB ceiling. Sets
 142:    * `GITNEXUS_MAX_FILE_SIZE` for the rest of the pipeline.
 143:    */
 144:   maxFileSize?: string;
 145:   /** Override worker sub-batch idle timeout in seconds. */
 146:   workerTimeout?: string;
 147:   embeddingThreads?: string;
 148:   embeddingBatchSize?: string;
 149:   embeddingSubBatchSize?: string;
 150:   embeddingDevice?: string;
 151: }
 152: 
 153: export const analyzeCommand = async (inputPath?: string, options?: AnalyzeOptions) => {
 154:   if (ensureHeap()) return;
 155: 
 156:   // Install fatal handlers immediately after re-exec resolution so any
 157:   // async error that escapes the try/catch below (#1169) surfaces with
 158:   // a stack trace and a non-zero exit code instead of a silent exit 0.
 159:   installFatalHandlers();
 160: 
 161:   if (options?.verbose) {
 162:     process.env.GITNEXUS_VERBOSE = '1';
 163:   }
 164: 
 165:   if (options?.maxFileSize) {
 166:     process.env.GITNEXUS_MAX_FILE_SIZE = options.maxFileSize;
 167:   }
 168: 
 169:   if (options?.workerTimeout) {
 170:     const workerTimeoutSeconds = Number(options.workerTimeout);
 171:     if (!Number.isFinite(workerTimeoutSeconds) || workerTimeoutSeconds < 1) {
 172:       cliError('  --worker-timeout must be at least 1 second.\n');
 173:       process.exitCode = 1;
 174:       return;
 175:     }
 176:     process.env.GITNEXUS_WORKER_SUB_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS = String(
 177:       Math.round(workerTimeoutSeconds * 1000),
 178:     );
 179:   }
 180: 
 181:   // Parse `--embeddings [limit]`: `true` → default cap, string → numeric cap
 182:   // (0 disables the cap entirely). Validated up here so failures match the
 183:   // sibling-validation pattern (exit before bar.start() — otherwise
 184:   // process.exit() leaves the progress bar's hidden cursor uncleared).
 185:   let embeddingsNodeLimit: number | undefined;
 186:   if (typeof options?.embeddings === 'string') {
 187:     const parsed = Number(options.embeddings);
 188:     if (!Number.isInteger(parsed) || parsed < 0) {
 189:       cliError(
 190:         `  --embeddings expects a non-negative integer (got "${options.embeddings}"). ` +
 191:           `Pass 0 to disable the safety cap, or omit the value to keep the default.\n`,
 192:       );
 193:       process.exitCode = 1;
 194:       return;
 195:     }
 196:     embeddingsNodeLimit = parsed;
 197:   }
 198:   const embeddingsEnabled = !!options?.embeddings;
 199: 
 200:   const setPositiveEnv = (
 201:     optionName: string,
 202:     envName: string,
 203:     value: string | undefined,
 204:   ): boolean => {
 205:     if (value === undefined) return true;
 206:     const parsed = Number(value);
 207:     if (!Number.isInteger(parsed) || parsed <= 0) {
 208:       cliError(`  ${optionName} must be a positive integer.\n`);
 209:       process.exitCode = 1;
 210:       return false;
 211:     }
 212:     process.env[envName] = String(parsed);
 213:     return true;
 214:   };
 215: 
 216:   if (
 217:     !setPositiveEnv(
 218:       '--embedding-threads',
 219:       'GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_THREADS',
 220:       options?.embeddingThreads,
 221:     ) ||
 222:     !setPositiveEnv(
 223:       '--embedding-batch-size',
 224:       'GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_BATCH_SIZE',
 225:       options?.embeddingBatchSize,
 226:     ) ||
 227:     !setPositiveEnv(
 228:       '--embedding-sub-batch-size',
 229:       'GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_SUB_BATCH_SIZE',
 230:       options?.embeddingSubBatchSize,
 231:     )
 232:   ) {
 233:     return;
 234:   }
 235: 
 236:   if (options?.embeddingDevice) {
 237:     const allowed = new Set(['auto', 'cpu', 'dml', 'cuda', 'wasm']);
 238:     if (!allowed.has(options.embeddingDevice)) {
 239:       cliError('  --embedding-device must be one of: auto, cpu, dml, cuda, wasm.\n');
 240:       process.exitCode = 1;

 241:       return;
 242:     }
 243:     process.env.GITNEXUS_EMBEDDING_DEVICE = options.embeddingDevice;
 244:   }
 245: 
 246:   console.log('\n  GitNexus Analyzer\n');
 247: 
 248:   let repoPath: string;
 249:   if (inputPath) {
 250:     repoPath = path.resolve(inputPath);
 251:   } else if (options?.skipGit) {
 252:     // --skip-git: treat cwd as the index root, do not walk up to a parent git repo.
 253:     repoPath = path.resolve(process.cwd());
 254:   } else {
 255:     const gitRoot = getGitRoot(process.cwd());
 256:     if (!gitRoot) {
 257:       console.log(
 258:         '  Not inside a git repository.\n  Tip: pass --skip-git to index any folder without a .git directory.\n',
 259:       );
 260:       process.exitCode = 1;
 261:       return;
 262:     }
 263:     repoPath = gitRoot;
 264:   }
 265: 
 266:   const repoHasGit = hasGitDir(repoPath);
 267:   if (!repoHasGit && !options?.skipGit) {
 268:     console.log(
 269:       '  Not a git repository.\n  Tip: pass --skip-git to index any folder without a .git directory.\n',
 270:     );
 271:     process.exitCode = 1;
 272:     return;
 273:   }
 274:   if (!repoHasGit) {
 275:     console.log(
 276:       '  Warning: no .git directory found \u2014 commit-tracking and incremental updates disabled.\n',
 277:     );
 278:   }
 279: 
 280:   // If the target repo contains files an optional grammar would parse but
 281:   // that grammar's native binding is absent, warn before analysis so users
 282:   // learn why those files end up unparsed instead of silently getting a
 283:   // degraded index.
 284:   try {
 285:     const matches = await glob(['**/*.dart', '**/*.proto'], {
 286:       cwd: repoPath,
 287:       ignore: ['**/node_modules/**', '**/.git/**', '**/dist/**', '**/build/**'],
 288:       dot: false,
 289:       nodir: true,
 290:       absolute: false,
 291:     });
 292:     if (matches.length > 0) {
 293:       const present = new Set<string>();
 294:       for (const m of matches) {
 295:         const ext = path.extname(m).toLowerCase();
 296:         if (ext) present.add(ext);
 297:       }
 298:       warnMissingOptionalGrammars({ context: 'analyze', relevantExtensions: present });
 299:     }
 300:   } catch {
 301:     // Best-effort warning \u2014 never block analyze on the precheck.
 302:   }
 303: 
 304:   // KuzuDB migration cleanup is handled by runFullAnalysis internally.
 305:   // Note: --skills is handled after runFullAnalysis using the returned pipelineResult.
 306: 
 307:   if (process.env.GITNEXUS_NO_GITIGNORE) {
 308:     console.log(
 309:       '  GITNEXUS_NO_GITIGNORE is set — skipping .gitignore (still reading .gitnexusignore)\n',
 310:     );
 311:   }
 312: 
 313:   const maxFileSizeBanner = getMaxFileSizeBannerMessage();
 314:   if (maxFileSizeBanner) {
 315:     console.log(`${maxFileSizeBanner}\n`);
 316:   }
 317: 
 318:   // ── CLI progress bar setup ─────────────────────────────────────────
 319:   const bar = new cliProgress.SingleBar(
 320:     {
 321:       format: '  {bar} {percentage}% | {phase}',
 322:       barCompleteChar: '\u2588',
 323:       barIncompleteChar: '\u2591',
 324:       hideCursor: true,
 325:       barGlue: '',
 326:       autopadding: true,
 327:       clearOnComplete: false,
 328:       stopOnComplete: false,
 329:     },
 330:     cliProgress.Presets.shades_grey,
 331:   );
 332: 
 333:   bar.start(100, 0, { phase: 'Initializing...' });
 334: 
 335:   // Graceful SIGINT handling. Pino's default destination is `sync: false`
 336:   // (buffered) — flush before exit so in-flight records reach stderr.
 337:   // See `gitnexus/src/core/logger.ts:flushLoggerSync`.
 338:   let aborted = false;
 339:   const sigintHandler = () => {
 340:     if (aborted) process.exit(1);
 341:     aborted = true;
 342:     bar.stop();
 343:     console.log('\n  Interrupted — cleaning up...');
 344:     closeLbug()
 345:       .catch(() => {})
 346:       .finally(async () => {
 347:         const { flushLoggerSync } = await import('../core/logger.js');
 348:         flushLoggerSync();
 349:         process.exit(130);
 350:       });
 351:   };
 352:   process.on('SIGINT', sigintHandler);
 353: 
 354:   // Route console output through bar.log() to prevent progress bar corruption.
 355:   // This is a deliberate UI pattern (not a logging concern): analyze runs a
 356:   // long-lived progress bar on stdout; any concurrent console.* write would
 357:   // overwrite the bar mid-render. We capture originals, swap to barLog for
 358:   // the lifetime of the run, and restore on completion/error/SIGINT.
 359:   const origLog = console.log.bind(console);
 360:   // eslint-disable-next-line no-console -- intentional console-routing for progress bar UX
 361:   const origWarn = console.warn.bind(console);
 362:   // eslint-disable-next-line no-console -- intentional console-routing for progress bar UX
 363:   const origError = console.error.bind(console);
 364:   let barCurrentValue = 0;
 365:   const barLog = (...args: any[]) => {
 366:     process.stdout.write('\x1b[2K\r');
 367:     origLog(args.map((a) => (typeof a === 'string' ? a : String(a))).join(' '));
 368:     bar.update(barCurrentValue);
 369:   };
 370:   console.log = barLog;
 371:   // eslint-disable-next-line no-console -- intentional console-routing for progress bar UX
 372:   console.warn = barLog;
 373:   // eslint-disable-next-line no-console -- intentional console-routing for progress bar UX
 374:   console.error = barLog;
 375: 
 376:   // Track elapsed time per phase
 377:   let lastPhaseLabel = 'Initializing...';
 378:   let phaseStart = Date.now();
 379: 
 380:   const updateBar = (value: number, phaseLabel: string) => {

 381:     barCurrentValue = value;
 382:     if (phaseLabel !== lastPhaseLabel) {
 383:       lastPhaseLabel = phaseLabel;
 384:       phaseStart = Date.now();
 385:     }
 386:     const elapsed = Math.round((Date.now() - phaseStart) / 1000);
 387:     const display = elapsed >= 3 ? `${phaseLabel} (${elapsed}s)` : phaseLabel;
 388:     bar.update(value, { phase: display });
 389:   };
 390: 
 391:   const elapsedTimer = setInterval(() => {
 392:     const elapsed = Math.round((Date.now() - phaseStart) / 1000);
 393:     if (elapsed >= 3) {
 394:       bar.update({ phase: `${lastPhaseLabel} (${elapsed}s)` });
 395:     }
 396:   }, 1000);
 397: 
 398:   const t0 = Date.now();
 399: 
 400:   // ── Run shared analysis orchestrator ───────────────────────────────
 401:   try {
 402:     const result = await runFullAnalysis(
 403:       repoPath,
 404:       {
 405:         // Pipeline re-index — OR'd with --skills because skill generation
 406:         // needs a fresh pipelineResult. Has no bearing on the registry
 407:         // collision guard (see allowDuplicateName below).
 408:         force: options?.force || options?.skills,
 409:         embeddings: embeddingsEnabled,
 410:         embeddingsNodeLimit,
 411:         dropEmbeddings: options?.dropEmbeddings,
 412:         skipGit: options?.skipGit,
 413:         skipAgentsMd: options?.skipAgentsMd,
 414:         noStats: options?.noStats,
 415:         registryName: options?.name,
 416:         // Registry-collision bypass — its own CLI flag, intentionally NOT
 417:         // overloading --force. A user who hits the collision guard should
 418:         // be able to accept the duplicate name without also paying the
 419:         // cost of a full pipeline re-index. See #829 review round 2.
 420:         allowDuplicateName: options?.allowDuplicateName,
 421:       },
 422:       {
 423:         onProgress: (_phase, percent, message) => {
 424:           updateBar(percent, message);
 425:         },
 426:         onLog: barLog,
 427:       },
 428:     );
 429: 
 430:     if (result.alreadyUpToDate) {
 431:       // Even the fast path must prove the repo is discoverable. A prior
 432:       // run can write meta.json and then fail before registerRepo(); in
 433:       // that half-finalized state, runFullAnalysis returns alreadyUpToDate
 434:       // on the next invocation unless we check the registry here too.
 435:       await assertAnalysisFinalized(repoPath);
 436:       clearInterval(elapsedTimer);
 437:       process.removeListener('SIGINT', sigintHandler);
 438:       console.log = origLog;
 439:       // eslint-disable-next-line no-console -- restoring after intentional progress-bar routing
 440:       console.warn = origWarn;
 441:       // eslint-disable-next-line no-console -- restoring after intentional progress-bar routing
 442:       console.error = origError;
 443:       bar.stop();
 444:       console.log('  Already up to date\n');
 445:       // Safe to return without process.exit(0) — the early-return path in
 446:       // runFullAnalysis never opens LadybugDB, so no native handles prevent exit.
 447:       return;
 448:     }
 449: 
 450:     // Post-finalize invariant (#1169): runFullAnalysis nominally writes
 451:     // meta.json and registers the repo, but on Windows it has been
 452:     // observed to return successfully with neither artifact present
 453:     // (banner-only output, exit 0). Verify both before declaring
 454:     // success so the silent-finalize state surfaces with a non-zero
 455:     // exit code and an actionable error instead of being mistaken for
 456:     // a healthy index.
 457:     await assertAnalysisFinalized(repoPath);
 458: 
 459:     // Skill generation (CLI-only, uses pipeline result from analysis)
 460:     if (options?.skills && result.pipelineResult) {
 461:       updateBar(99, 'Generating skill files...');
 462:       try {
 463:         const { generateSkillFiles } = await import('./skill-gen.js');
 464:         const { generateAIContextFiles } = await import('./ai-context.js');
 465:         const skillResult = await generateSkillFiles(
 466:           repoPath,
 467:           result.repoName,
 468:           result.pipelineResult,
 469:         );
 470:         if (skillResult.skills.length > 0) {
 471:           barLog(`  Generated ${skillResult.skills.length} skill files`);
 472:           // Re-generate AI context files now that we have skill info
 473:           const s = result.stats;
 474:           const communityResult = result.pipelineResult?.communityResult;
 475:           let aggregatedClusterCount = 0;
 476:           if (communityResult?.communities) {
 477:             const groups = new Map<string, number>();
 478:             for (const c of communityResult.communities) {
 479:               const label = c.heuristicLabel || c.label || 'Unknown';
 480:               groups.set(label, (groups.get(label) || 0) + c.symbolCount);
 481:             }
 482:             aggregatedClusterCount = Array.from(groups.values()).filter(
 483:               (count: number) => count >= 5,
 484:             ).length;
 485:           }
 486:           const { storagePath: sp } = getStoragePaths(repoPath);
 487:           await generateAIContextFiles(
 488:             repoPath,
 489:             sp,
 490:             result.repoName,
 491:             {
 492:               files: s.files ?? 0,
 493:               nodes: s.nodes ?? 0,
 494:               edges: s.edges ?? 0,
 495:               communities: s.communities,
 496:               clusters: aggregatedClusterCount,
 497:               processes: s.processes,
 498:             },
 499:             skillResult.skills,
 500:             { skipAgentsMd: options?.skipAgentsMd, noStats: options?.noStats },
 501:           );
 502:         }
 503:       } catch {
 504:         /* best-effort */
 505:       }
 506:     }
 507: 
 508:     const totalTime = ((Date.now() - t0) / 1000).toFixed(1);
 509: 
 510:     clearInterval(elapsedTimer);
 511:     process.removeListener('SIGINT', sigintHandler);
 512: 
 513:     console.log = origLog;
 514:     // eslint-disable-next-line no-console -- restoring after intentional progress-bar routing
 515:     console.warn = origWarn;
 516:     // eslint-disable-next-line no-console -- restoring after intentional progress-bar routing
 517:     console.error = origError;
 518: 
 519:     bar.update(100, { phase: 'Done' });
 520:     bar.stop();
 521: 
 522:     // ── Summary ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 523:     const s = result.stats;
 524:     console.log(`\n  Repository indexed successfully (${totalTime}s)\n`);
 525:     console.log(
 526:       `  ${(s.nodes ?? 0).toLocaleString()} nodes | ${(s.edges ?? 0).toLocaleString()} edges | ${s.communities ?? 0} clusters | ${s.processes ?? 0} flows`,
 527:     );
 528:     console.log(`  ${repoPath}`);
 529: 
 530:     try {
 531:       await fs.access(getGlobalRegistryPath());
 532:     } catch {
 533:       console.log('\n  Tip: Run `gitnexus setup` to configure MCP for your editor.');
 534:     }
 535: 
 536:     console.log('');
 537:   } catch (err: any) {
 538:     clearInterval(elapsedTimer);
 539:     process.removeListener('SIGINT', sigintHandler);
 540:     console.log = origLog;

 541:     // eslint-disable-next-line no-console -- restoring after intentional progress-bar routing
 542:     console.warn = origWarn;
 543:     // eslint-disable-next-line no-console -- restoring after intentional progress-bar routing
 544:     console.error = origError;
 545:     bar.stop();
 546: 
 547:     const msg = err.message || String(err);
 548: 
 549:     // Registry name-collision from --name (#829) — surface as an
 550:     // actionable error rather than a generic stack-trace.
 551:     if (err instanceof RegistryNameCollisionError) {
 552:       cliError(
 553:         `\n  Registry name collision:\n` +
 554:           `    "${err.registryName}" is already used by "${err.existingPath}".\n\n` +
 555:           `  Options:\n` +
 556:           `    • Pick a different alias:  gitnexus analyze --name <alias>\n` +
 557:           `    • Allow the duplicate:     gitnexus analyze --allow-duplicate-name  (leaves "-r ${err.registryName}" ambiguous)\n`,
 558:         { registryName: err.registryName, existingPath: err.existingPath },
 559:       );
 560:       process.exitCode = 1;
 561:       return;
 562:     }
 563: 
 564:     // Finalize invariant failure (#1169) — keep the rich actionable
 565:     // message intact and write through realStderrWrite so it can't be
 566:     // erased by a leftover bar refresh on slow terminals.
 567:     if (err instanceof AnalysisNotFinalizedError) {
 568:       writeFatalToStderr('Analysis did not finalize', err);
 569:       realStderrWrite(
 570:         `\n  Diagnostic checklist:\n` +
 571:           `    1. Re-run "gitnexus analyze" - transient native errors often clear on retry.\n` +
 572:           `    2. Inspect ${err.storagePath} - a leftover lbug.wal indicates an aborted write.\n` +
 573:           `    3. If the failure persists, run with NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=8192 --trace-exit"\n` +
 574:           `       and attach the trace to the GitNexus issue tracker.\n\n`,
 575:       );
 576:       process.exitCode = 1;
 577:       return;
 578:     }
 579: 
 580:     // HF download failure — show clean guidance without the raw stack trace.
 581:     // Checked before writeFatalToStderr so the user sees one focused message
 582:     // rather than a stack-trace dump followed by a second remediation block.
 583:     if (isHfDownloadFailure(msg) || msg.includes('Failed to download embedding model')) {
 584:       cliError(
 585:         `  The embedding model could not be downloaded.\n` +
 586:           `  huggingface.co may be unreachable from your network\n` +
 587:           `  (e.g. behind a corporate proxy or a regional firewall).\n` +
 588:           `  Suggestions:\n` +
 589:           `    1. Set HF_ENDPOINT to a mirror and retry:\n` +
 590:           `         HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings\n` +
 591:           `         (Windows: set HF_ENDPOINT=https://hf-mirror.com && npx gitnexus analyze --embeddings)\n` +
 592:           `    2. Check your proxy / VPN settings.\n` +
 593:           `    3. Once downloaded the model is cached — future runs work offline.\n`,
 594:         { recoveryHint: 'hf-endpoint-unreachable' },
 595:       );
 596:       process.exitCode = 1;
 597:       return;
 598:     }
 599: 
 600:     // Bypass the redirected console.error and write the full stack to
 601:     // the real stderr captured at module load. The redirected
 602:     // console.error wraps every line with `\\x1b[2K\\r` (ANSI clear-line)
 603:     // and forces a bar.update() afterwards, which on some Windows
 604:     // terminals visually erases the failure message — the canonical
 605:     // shape of the silent-exit symptom in #1169.
 606:     writeFatalToStderr('Analysis failed', err);
 607: 
 608:     // Provide helpful guidance for known failure modes
 609:     if (
 610:       msg.includes('Maximum call stack size exceeded') ||
 611:       msg.includes('call stack') ||
 612:       msg.includes('Map maximum size') ||
 613:       msg.includes('Invalid array length') ||
 614:       msg.includes('Invalid string length') ||
 615:       msg.includes('allocation failed') ||
 616:       msg.includes('heap out of memory') ||
 617:       msg.includes('JavaScript heap')
 618:     ) {
 619:       cliError(
 620:         `  This error typically occurs on very large repositories.\n` +
 621:           `  Suggestions:\n` +
 622:           `    1. Add large vendored/generated directories to .gitnexusignore\n` +
 623:           `    2. Increase Node.js heap: NODE_OPTIONS="--max-old-space-size=16384"\n` +
 624:           `    3. Increase stack size: NODE_OPTIONS="--stack-size=4096"\n`,
 625:         { recoveryHint: 'large-repo' },
 626:       );
 627:     } else if (msg.includes('ERESOLVE') || msg.includes('Could not resolve dependency')) {
 628:       // Note: the original arborist "Cannot destructure property 'package' of
 629:       // 'node.target'" crash happens inside npm *before* gitnexus code runs,
 630:       // so it can't be caught here.  This branch handles dependency-resolution
 631:       // errors that surface at runtime (e.g. dynamic require failures).
 632:       cliError(
 633:         `  This looks like an npm dependency resolution issue.\n` +
 634:           `  Suggestions:\n` +
 635:           `    1. Clear the npm cache:    npm cache clean --force\n` +

   1: /**
   2:  * Remove Command (#664)
   3:  *
   4:  * Delete the `.gitnexus/` index for a registered repo and unregister it
   5:  * from the global registry (~/.gitnexus/registry.json). The target is
   6:  * identified by alias / basename-derived name / remote-inferred name /
   7:  * absolute path — no `--repo` flag, just a positional argument so the
   8:  * destructive-command ergonomics match `clean` (which is also
   9:  * destructive but scoped to `process.cwd()`).
  10:  *
  11:  * Compared to `clean`:
  12:  *   - `clean`  acts on the repo discovered by walking up from cwd.
  13:  *   - `remove` acts on any registered repo identified by name or path.
  14:  *
  15:  * Behaviour notes:
  16:  *   - Idempotent on unknown targets: exits 0 with a warning so that
  17:  *     `remove X && analyze Y` keeps working in scripts. Per #664:
  18:  *     "behave atomically and idempotently so retries are safe".
  19:  *   - Atomic order mirrors `clean`: fs.rm FIRST, then unregister. A
  20:  *     partial failure leaves the registry pointing at a missing dir
  21:  *     (recoverable by `listRegisteredRepos({ validate: true })` on
  22:  *     next read) rather than the opposite, which would orphan
  23:  *     .gitnexus/ directories on disk.
  24:  *   - `-f` / `--force` matches the confirmation-skip semantics of
  25:  *     `clean -f`. (Distinct from `analyze --force`, which re-indexes;
  26:  *     here there is no pipeline, so no conflation.)
  27:  */
  28: 
  29: import fs from 'fs/promises';
  30: import { logger } from '../core/logger.js';
  31: import { cliError } from './cli-message.js';
  32: import {
  33:   readRegistry,
  34:   resolveRegistryEntry,
  35:   assertSafeStoragePath,
  36:   unregisterRepo,
  37:   RegistryNotFoundError,
  38:   RegistryAmbiguousTargetError,
  39:   UnsafeStoragePathError,
  40: } from '../storage/repo-manager.js';
  41: 
  42: export const removeCommand = async (target: string, options?: { force?: boolean }) => {
  43:   // Read the registry snapshot once and pass it to the resolver — this
  44:   // lets us render the "before" state in the dry-run path without a
  45:   // second disk read.
  46:   const entries = await readRegistry();
  47: 
  48:   let entry;
  49:   try {
  50:     entry = resolveRegistryEntry(entries, target);
  51:   } catch (err) {
  52:     if (err instanceof RegistryNotFoundError) {
  53:       // Idempotent: missing target is a no-op warning, not an error.
  54:       // The `availableNames` hint comes from the error itself so users
  55:       // can see what they might have meant.
  56:       logger.warn(`Nothing to remove: ${err.message}`);
  57:       return;
  58:     }
  59:     if (err instanceof RegistryAmbiguousTargetError) {
  60:       // Duplicate aliases are allowed via --allow-duplicate-name (#829);
  61:       // refuse to guess which one the user meant — surface the full list
  62:       // and exit non-zero so scripts don't silently pick the wrong repo.
  63:       cliError(`Error: ${err.message}`);
  64:       process.exit(1);
  65:     }
  66:     throw err;
  67:   }
  68: 
  69:   // Confirmation gate — same shape as `clean`. Default is a dry-run
  70:   // that describes what would be deleted; `--force` actually deletes.
  71:   if (!options?.force) {
  72:     console.log(`This will delete the GitNexus index for: ${entry.name}`);
  73:     console.log(`   Path:    ${entry.path}`);
  74:     console.log(`   Storage: ${entry.storagePath}`);
  75:     console.log('\nRun with --force to confirm deletion.');
  76:     return;
  77:   }
  78: 
  79:   // Safety guard (#1003 review — @magyargergo): refuse to proceed if
  80:   // the registry entry's `storagePath` isn't the canonical
  81:   // `<entry.path>/.gitnexus` subfolder. `~/.gitnexus/registry.json` is
  82:   // user-writable, so a corrupted or hand-edited entry could point
  83:   // storagePath at the repo root, an empty string (→ cwd), a parent
  84:   // dir, or anywhere else; `fs.rm(recursive: true, force: true)` on
  85:   // any of those would be a runtime disaster. Bail before touching
  86:   // disk, with an actionable hint for recovering a broken registry.
  87:   try {
  88:     assertSafeStoragePath(entry);
  89:   } catch (err) {
  90:     if (err instanceof UnsafeStoragePathError) {
  91:       cliError(`Error: ${err.message}`);
  92:       process.exit(1);
  93:     }
  94:     throw err;
  95:   }
  96: 
  97:   // Deletion order: fs.rm first, then unregister. If fs.rm fails mid-way,
  98:   // the registry entry stays so the user can retry. If fs.rm succeeds but
  99:   // unregister throws (e.g. ENOSPC on registry write), the entry becomes
 100:   // orphaned — `listRegisteredRepos({ validate: true })` prunes those on
 101:   // next read, so the failure is self-healing.
 102:   try {
 103:     await fs.rm(entry.storagePath, { recursive: true, force: true });
 104:     await unregisterRepo(entry.path);
 105:     console.log(`Removed: ${entry.name}`);
 106:     console.log(`   Path:    ${entry.path}`);
 107:     console.log(`   Storage: ${entry.storagePath}`);
 108:   } catch (err) {
 109:     const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
 110:     cliError(`Failed to remove ${entry.name}: ${msg}`, { err });
 111:     process.exit(1);
 112:   }
 113: };

   4:  * Fast-path command for platform hooks.
   5:  * Shells out from Claude Code PreToolUse / Cursor beforeShellExecution hooks.
   6:  *
   7:  * Usage: gitnexus augment <pattern>
   8:  * Returns enriched text to stdout.
   9:  *
  10:  * Performance: Must cold-start fast (<500ms).
  11:  * Skips unnecessary initialization (no web server, no full DB warmup).
  12:  */
  13: 
  14: import { augment } from '../core/augmentation/engine.js';
  15: 
  16: export async function augmentCommand(pattern: string): Promise<void> {

  18:     process.exit(0);
  19:   }
  20: 
  21:   try {
  22:     const result = await augment(pattern, process.cwd());
  23: 
  24:     if (result) {
  25:       // IMPORTANT: Write to stderr, NOT stdout.
  26:       // LadybugDB's native module captures stdout fd at OS level during init,
  27:       // which makes stdout permanently broken in subprocess contexts.
  28:       // stderr is never captured, so it works reliably everywhere.
  29:       // The hook reads from the subprocess's stderr.
  30:       process.stderr.write(result + '\n');
  31:     }
  32:   } catch {
  33:     // Graceful failure — never break the calling hook
  34:     process.exit(0);
  35:   }
  36: }

  25:   force?: boolean;
  26:   model?: string;
  27:   baseUrl?: string;
  28:   apiKey?: string;
  29:   apiVersion?: string;
  30:   reasoningModel?: boolean;
  31:   concurrency?: string;
  32:   gist?: boolean;
  33:   provider?: LLMProvider;
  34:   verbose?: boolean;
  35:   review?: boolean;

  38: /**
  39:  * Prompt the user for input via stdin.
  40:  */
  41: function prompt(question: string, hide = false): Promise<string> {
  42:   return new Promise((resolve) => {
  43:     const rl = readline.createInterface({
  44:       input: process.stdin,
  45:       output: process.stdout,
  46:     });
  47: 
  48:     if (hide && process.stdin.isTTY) {
  49:       // Mask input for API keys
  50:       process.stdout.write(question);
  51:       let input = '';
  52:       process.stdin.setRawMode(true);
  53:       process.stdin.resume();
  54:       process.stdin.setEncoding('utf-8');
  55: 
  56:       const onData = (char: string) => {
  57:         if (char === '\n' || char === '\r' || char === '\u0004') {
  58:           process.stdin.setRawMode(false);
  59:           process.stdin.removeListener('data', onData);
  60:           process.stdout.write('\n');
  61:           rl.close();
  62:           resolve(input);
  63:         } else if (char === '\u0003') {
  64:           // Ctrl+C
  65:           process.stdin.setRawMode(false);
  66:           rl.close();
  67:           process.exit(1);
  68:         } else if (char === '\u007F' || char === '\b') {
  69:           // Backspace
  70:           if (input.length > 0) {
  71:             input = input.slice(0, -1);
  72:             process.stdout.write('\b \b');
  73:           }
  74:         } else {
  75:           input += char;
  76:           process.stdout.write('*');
  77:         }
  78:       };
  79:       process.stdin.on('data', onData);
  80:     } else {
  81:       rl.question(question, (answer) => {
  82:         rl.close();
  83:         resolve(answer.trim());
  84:       });
  85:     }
  86:   });
  87: }

 469:         }

 474:       bar.start(100, 30, { phase: 'Generating pages...' });
 475: 
 476:       // Re-run generator without reviewOnly flag
 477:       const continueOptions: WikiOptions = {
 478:         ...wikiOptions,
 479:         reviewOnly: false,
 480:       };
 481: 
 482:       const continueGenerator = new WikiGenerator(
 483:         repoPath,

 516:

 520:     }
 521: 
 522:     bar.update(100, { phase: 'Done' });

 524:     if (result.mode === 'up-to-date' && !options?.force) {

 529:     }
 530: 
 531:     console.log(`\n  Wiki generated successfully (${elapsed}s)\n`);
 532:     console.log(`  Mode: ${result.mode}`);
 533:     console.log(`  Pages: ${result.pagesGenerated}`);
 534:     console.log(`  Output: ${wikiDir}`);
 535:     console.log(`  Viewer: ${viewerPath}`);
 536: 
 537:     if (result.failedModules && result.failedModules.length > 0) {
 538:       console.log(`\n  Failed modules (${result.failedModules.length}):`);
 539:       for (const mod of result.failedModules) {
 540:         console.log(`    - ${mod}`);
 541:       }
 542:       console.log('  Re-run to retry failed modules (pages will be regenerated).');
 543:     }
 544: 
 545:     console.log('');
 546: 
 547:     await maybePublishGist(viewerPath, options?.gist);
 548:   } catch (err: any) {
 549:     clearInterval(elapsedTimer);
 550:     bar.stop();
 551: 
 552:     if (err.message?.includes('No source files')) {
 553:       console.log(`\n  ${err.message}\n`);
 554:     } else if (err.message?.includes('content filter')) {
 555:       // Content filter block — actionable message
 556:       console.log(`\n  Content Filter: ${err.message}\n`);
 557:       console.log(
 558:         '  To resolve: rephrase your prompt or adjust the content filter policy for your deployment.\n',
 559:       );
 560:     } else if (err.message?.includes('API key') || err.message?.includes('API error')) {
 561:       console.log(`\n  LLM Error: ${err.message}\n`);
 562: 
 563:       // Offer to reconfigure on auth-related failures
 564:       const isAuthError =
 565:         err.message?.includes('401') ||
 566:         err.message?.includes('403') ||
 567:         err.message?.includes('502') ||
 568:         err.message?.includes('authenticate') ||
 569:         err.message?.includes('Unauthorized');
 570:       if (isAuthError && process.stdin.isTTY) {
 571:         const answer = await new Promise<string>((resolve) => {
 572:           const rl = readline.createInterface({ input: process.stdin, output: process.stdout });
 573:           rl.question('  Reconfigure LLM settings? (Y/n): ', (ans) => {
 574:             rl.close();
 575:             resolve(ans.trim().toLowerCase());
 576:           });
 577:         });
 578:         if (!answer || answer === 'y' || answer === 'yes') {
 579:           // Clear saved config so next run triggers interactive setup
 580:           await saveCLIConfig({});
 581:           console.log('  Config cleared. Run `gitnexus wiki` again to reconfigure.\n');
 582:         }
 583:       }
 584:     } else {
 585:       console.log(`\n  Error: ${err.message}\n`);
 586:       if (process.env.GITNEXUS_VERBOSE) {
 587:         logger.error({ err }, 'wiki command failed');
 588:       }
 589:     }
 590:     process.exitCode = 1;
 591:   }
 592: };

 594: // ─── Gist Publishing ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
 595: 
 596: function hasGhCLI(): boolean {
 597:   try {
 598:     execSync('gh --version', { stdio: 'ignore' });
 599:     return true;
 600:   } catch {
 601:     return false;
 602:   }
 603: }
 604: 
 605: /**
 606:  * Strict Gist URL predicate. Rejects:
 607:  *   - any URL that does not parse (URL constructor throws)
 608:  *   - schemes other than https (drops `http:`, `file:`, `gist:`-style spoofs)
 609:  *   - hostnames that are not exactly `gist.github.com` (drops substring spoofs
 610:  *     like `https://evil.com/?u=gist.github.com` and userinfo-prefixed shapes
 611:  *     like `https://[email protected]/...` — note that URL.hostname
 612:  *     strips userinfo, so the equality check rejects the userinfo-prefixed
 613:  *     spoof if the actual host differs from gist.github.com)
 614:  *   - any URL containing userinfo (`username[:password]@`), which the URL
 615:  *     parser exposes via `.username` / `.password`. Defense-in-depth: even
 616:  *     when hostname matches, a credential-bearing URL is suspect and not
 617:  *     produced by `gh gist create`.
 618:  *
 619:  * Closes the substring-bypass class CodeQL `js/incomplete-url-substring-
 620:  * sanitization` flags.

 621:  */
 622: function isGistUrl(line: string): boolean {
 623:   const trimmed = line.trim();
 624:   try {
 625:     const u = new URL(trimmed);
 626:     return (
 627:       u.protocol === 'https:' &&
 628:       u.hostname === 'gist.github.com' &&
 629:       u.username === '' &&
 630:       u.password === ''
 631:     );
 632:   } catch {
 633:     return false;
 634:   }
 635: }
 636: 
 637: function publishGist(htmlPath: string): { url: string; rawUrl: string } | null {
 638:   try {
 639:     const output = execFileSync(
 640:       'gh',
 641:       ['gist', 'create', htmlPath, '--desc', 'Repository Wiki — generated by GitNexus', '--public'],
 642:       { encoding: 'utf-8', stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'] },
 643:     ).trim();
 644: 
 645:     // `gh gist create` prints the gist URL as a line in the output. Find the
 646:     // first parseable Gist URL — if no line is a valid Gist URL, fail closed
 647:     // (do NOT fall back to lines[last]: a non-Gist last line would propagate
 648:     // through the regex below and produce a malformed `rawUrl`).
 649:     const gistUrl = output.split('\n').find(isGistUrl);
 650:     if (!gistUrl) return null;
 651: 
 652:     // Build a raw viewer URL via gist.githack.com.
 653:     // gist URL format: https://gist.github.com/{user}/{id}
 654:     const match = gistUrl.match(/gist\.github\.com\/([^/]+)\/([a-f0-9]+)/);
 655:     let rawUrl = gistUrl;
 656:     if (match) {
 657:       rawUrl = `https://gistcdn.githack.com/${match[1]}/${match[2]}/raw/index.html`;
 658:     }
 659: 
 660:     return { url: gistUrl.trim(), rawUrl };
 661:   } catch {
 662:     return null;
 663:   }
 664: }

 666: async function maybePublishGist(htmlPath: string, gistFlag?: boolean): Promise<void> {
 667:   if (gistFlag === false) return;
 668: 
 669:   // Check that the HTML file exists
 670:   try {

 673:   } catch {
 674:     return;
 675:   }
 676: 
 677:   if (!hasGhCLI()) {

 679:       console.log('  GitHub CLI (gh) is not installed. Cannot publish gist.');

 681:     }
 682:     return;
 683:   }
 684: 
 685:   let shouldPublish = !!gistFlag;
 686: 
 687:   if (!shouldPublish && process.stdin.isTTY) {
 688:     const answer = await new Promise<string>((resolve) => {
 689:       const rl = readline.createInterface({ input: process.stdin, output: process.stdout });
 690:       rl.question('  Publish wiki as a GitHub Gist for easy viewing? (Y/n): ', (ans) => {
 691:         rl.close();
 692:         resolve(ans.trim().toLowerCase());
 693:       });
 694:     });
 695:     shouldPublish = !answer || answer === 'y' || answer === 'yes';
 696:   }
 697: 
 698:   if (!shouldPublish) return;
 699: 
 700:   console.log('\n  Publishing to GitHub Gist...');
 701:   const result = publishGist(htmlPath);
 702: 
 703:   if (result) {
 704:     console.log(`  Gist:   ${result.url}`);
 705:     console.log(`  Viewer: ${result.rawUrl}\n`);
 706:   } else {
 707:     console.log('  Failed to publish gist. Make sure `gh auth login` is configured.\n');
 708:   }
 709: }

   1: /**
   2:  * Eval Server — Lightweight HTTP server for SWE-bench evaluation
   3:  *
   4:  * Keeps LadybugDB warm in memory so tool calls from the agent are near-instant.
   5:  * Designed to run inside Docker containers during SWE-bench evaluation.
   6:  *
   7:  * KEY DESIGN: Returns LLM-friendly text, not raw JSON.
   8:  * Raw JSON wastes tokens and is hard for models to parse. The text formatter
   9:  * converts structured results into compact, readable output that models
  10:  * can immediately act on. Next-step hints guide the agent through a
  11:  * productive tool-chaining workflow (query → context → impact → fix).
  12:  *
  13:  * Architecture:
  14:  *   Agent bash cmd → curl localhost:PORT/tool/query → eval-server → LocalBackend → format → text
  15:  *
  16:  * Usage:
  17:  *   gitnexus eval-server                    # default port 4848
  18:  *   gitnexus eval-server --port 4848        # explicit port
  19:  *   gitnexus eval-server --idle-timeout 300 # auto-shutdown after 300s idle
  20:  *
  21:  * API:
  22:  *   POST /tool/:name   — Call a tool. Body is JSON arguments. Returns formatted text.
  23:  *   GET  /health       — Health check. Returns {"status":"ok","repos":[...]}
  24:  *   POST /shutdown     — Graceful shutdown.
  25:  */

  39: // Convert structured JSON results into compact, LLM-friendly text.

  42: export function formatQueryResult(result: any): string {
  43:   if (result.error) return `Error: ${result.error}`;
  44: 
  45:   const lines: string[] = [];
  46:   const processes = result.processes || [];
  47:   const symbols = result.process_symbols || [];
  48:   const defs = result.definitions || [];
  49: 
  50:   if (processes.length === 0 && defs.length === 0) {
  51:     return 'No matching execution flows found. Try a different search term or use grep.';
  52:   }
  53: 
  54:   lines.push(`Found ${processes.length} execution flow(s):\n`);
  55: 
  56:   for (let i = 0; i < processes.length; i++) {
  57:     const p = processes[i];
  58:     lines.push(`${i + 1}. ${p.summary} (${p.step_count} steps, ${p.symbol_count} symbols)`);
  59: 
  60:     // Show symbols belonging to this process
  61:     const procSymbols = symbols.filter((s: any) => s.process_id === p.id);
  62:     for (const s of procSymbols.slice(0, 6)) {
  63:       const loc = s.startLine ? `:${s.startLine}` : '';
  64:       lines.push(`   ${s.type} ${s.name} → ${s.filePath}${loc}`);
  65:     }
  66:     if (procSymbols.length > 6) {
  67:       lines.push(`   ... and ${procSymbols.length - 6} more`);
  68:     }
  69:     lines.push('');
  70:   }
  71: 
  72:   if (defs.length > 0) {
  73:     lines.push(`Standalone definitions:`);
  74:     for (const d of defs.slice(0, 8)) {
  75:       lines.push(`  ${d.type || 'Symbol'} ${d.name} → ${d.filePath || '?'}`);
  76:     }
  77:     if (defs.length > 8) lines.push(`  ... and ${defs.length - 8} more`);
  78:   }
  79: 
  80:   return lines.join('\n').trim();
  81: }

  83: export function formatContextResult(result: any): string {
  84:   if (result.error) return `Error: ${result.error}`;
  85: 
  86:   if (result.status === 'ambiguous') {
  87:     const lines = [
  88:       `Multiple symbols named '${result.candidates?.[0]?.name || '?'}'. Disambiguate with file path:\n`,
  89:     ];
  90:     for (const c of result.candidates || []) {
  91:       lines.push(`  ${c.kind} ${c.name} → ${c.filePath}:${c.line || '?'}  (uid: ${c.uid})`);
  92:     }
  93:     lines.push(`\nRe-run: gitnexus-context "${result.candidates?.[0]?.name}" "<file_path>"`);
  94:     return lines.join('\n');
  95:   }
  96: 
  97:   const sym = result.symbol;
  98:   if (!sym) return 'Symbol not found.';
  99: 
 100:   const lines: string[] = [];
 101:   const loc = sym.startLine ? `:${sym.startLine}-${sym.endLine}` : '';
 102:   lines.push(`${sym.kind} ${sym.name} → ${sym.filePath}${loc}`);
 103:   lines.push('');
 104: 
 105:   // Incoming refs (who calls/imports/extends this)
 106:   const incoming = result.incoming || {};
 107:   const incomingCount = Object.values(incoming).reduce(
 108:     (sum: number, arr: any) => sum + arr.length,
 109:     0,
 110:   ) as number;
 111:   if (incomingCount > 0) {
 112:     lines.push(`Called/imported by (${incomingCount}):`);
 113:     for (const [relType, refs] of Object.entries(incoming)) {
 114:       for (const ref of (refs as any[]).slice(0, 10)) {
 115:         lines.push(`  ← [${relType}] ${ref.kind} ${ref.name} → ${ref.filePath}`);
 116:       }
 117:     }
 118:     lines.push('');
 119:   }
 120: 
 121:   // Outgoing refs (what this calls/imports)
 122:   const outgoing = result.outgoing || {};
 123:   const outgoingCount = Object.values(outgoing).reduce(
 124:     (sum: number, arr: any) => sum + arr.length,
 125:     0,
 126:   ) as number;
 127:   if (outgoingCount > 0) {
 128:     lines.push(`Calls/imports (${outgoingCount}):`);
 129:     for (const [relType, refs] of Object.entries(outgoing)) {
 130:       for (const ref of (refs as any[]).slice(0, 10)) {

 131:         lines.push(`  → [${relType}] ${ref.kind} ${ref.name} → ${ref.filePath}`);
 132:       }
 133:     }
 134:     lines.push('');
 135:   }
 136: 
 137:   // Processes
 138:   const procs = result.processes || [];
 139:   if (procs.length > 0) {
 140:     lines.push(`Participates in ${procs.length} execution flow(s):`);
 141:     for (const p of procs) {
 142:       lines.push(`  • ${p.name} (step ${p.step_index}/${p.step_count})`);
 143:     }
 144:   }
 145: 
 146:   if (sym.content) {
 147:     lines.push('');
 148:     lines.push(`Source:`);
 149:     lines.push(sym.content);
 150:   }
 151: 
 152:   return lines.join('\n').trim();
 153: }

 155: export function formatImpactResult(result: any): string {
 156:   if (result.error) {
 157:     const suggestion = result.suggestion ? `\nSuggestion: ${result.suggestion}` : '';
 158:     return `Error: ${result.error}${suggestion}`;
 159:   }
 160: 
 161:   const target = result.target;
 162:   const direction = result.direction;
 163:   const byDepth = result.byDepth || {};
 164:   const total = result.impactedCount || 0;
 165: 
 166:   if (total === 0) {
 167:     return `${target?.name || '?'}: No ${direction} dependencies found. This symbol appears isolated.`;
 168:   }
 169: 
 170:   const lines: string[] = [];
 171:   const dirLabel =
 172:     direction === 'upstream' ? 'depends on this (will break if changed)' : 'this depends on';
 173:   lines.push(
 174:     `Blast radius for ${target?.kind || ''} ${target?.name} (${direction}): ${total} symbol(s) ${dirLabel}`,
 175:   );
 176:   if (result.partial) {
 177:     lines.push('⚠️  Partial results — graph traversal was interrupted. Deeper impacts may exist.');
 178:   }
 179:   lines.push('');
 180: 
 181:   const depthLabels: Record<number, string> = {
 182:     1: 'WILL BREAK (direct)',
 183:     2: 'LIKELY AFFECTED (indirect)',
 184:     3: 'MAY NEED TESTING (transitive)',
 185:   };
 186: 
 187:   for (const depth of [1, 2, 3]) {
 188:     const items = byDepth[depth];
 189:     if (!items || items.length === 0) continue;
 190: 
 191:     lines.push(`d=${depth}: ${depthLabels[depth] || ''} (${items.length})`);
 192:     for (const item of items.slice(0, 12)) {
 193:       const conf = item.confidence < 1 ? ` (conf: ${item.confidence})` : '';
 194:       lines.push(`  ${item.type} ${item.name} → ${item.filePath} [${item.relationType}]${conf}`);
 195:     }
 196:     if (items.length > 12) {
 197:       lines.push(`  ... and ${items.length - 12} more`);
 198:     }
 199:     lines.push('');
 200:   }
 201: 
 202:   return lines.join('\n').trim();
 203: }

 205: export function formatCypherResult(result: any): string {
 206:   if (result.error) return `Error: ${result.error}`;
 207: 
 208:   if (Array.isArray(result)) {
 209:     if (result.length === 0) return 'Query returned 0 rows.';
 210:     // Format as simple table
 211:     const keys = Object.keys(result[0]);
 212:     const lines: string[] = [`${result.length} row(s):\n`];
 213:     for (const row of result.slice(0, 30)) {
 214:       const parts = keys.map((k) => `${k}: ${row[k]}`);
 215:       lines.push(`  ${parts.join(' | ')}`);
 216:     }
 217:     if (result.length > 30) {
 218:       lines.push(`  ... ${result.length - 30} more rows`);
 219:     }
 220:     return lines.join('\n');
 221:   }
 222: 
 223:   return typeof result === 'string' ? result : JSON.stringify(result, null, 2);
 224: }

 226: export function formatDetectChangesResult(result: any): string {
 227:   if (result.error) return `Error: ${result.error}`;
 228: 
 229:   const summary = result.summary || {};
 230:   const lines: string[] = [];
 231: 
 232:   if (summary.changed_count === 0) {
 233:     return 'No changes detected.';
 234:   }
 235: 
 236:   lines.push(`Changes: ${summary.changed_files || 0} files, ${summary.changed_count || 0} symbols`);
 237:   lines.push(`Affected processes: ${summary.affected_count || 0}`);
 238:   lines.push(`Risk level: ${summary.risk_level || 'unknown'}\n`);
 239: 
 240:   const changed = result.changed_symbols || [];
 241:   if (changed.length > 0) {
 242:     lines.push(`Changed symbols:`);
 243:     for (const s of changed.slice(0, 15)) {
 244:       lines.push(`  ${s.type} ${s.name} → ${s.filePath}`);
 245:     }
 246:     if (changed.length > 15) lines.push(`  ... and ${changed.length - 15} more`);
 247:     lines.push('');
 248:   }
 249: 
 250:   const affected = result.affected_processes || [];
 251:   if (affected.length > 0) {
 252:     lines.push(`Affected execution flows:`);
 253:     for (const p of affected.slice(0, 10)) {
 254:       const steps = (p.changed_steps || []).map((s: any) => s.symbol).join(', ');
 255:       lines.push(`  • ${p.name} (${p.step_count} steps) — changed: ${steps}`);
 256:     }
 257:   }
 258: 
 259:   return lines.join('\n').trim();
 260: }

 301: // ─── Next-Step Hints ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
 302: // Guide the agent to the logical next tool call.
 303: // Critical for tool chaining: query → context → impact → fix.
 304: 
 305: function getNextStepHint(toolName: string): string {
 306:   switch (toolName) {
 307:     case 'query':
 308:       return '\n---\nNext: Pick a symbol above and run gitnexus-context "<name>" to see all its callers, callees, and execution flows.';
 309: 
 310:     case 'context':
 311:       return '\n---\nNext: To check what breaks if you change this, run gitnexus-impact "<name>" upstream';
 312: 
 313:     case 'impact':
 314:       return '\n---\nNext: Review d=1 items first (WILL BREAK). Read the source with cat to understand the code, then make your fix.';
 315: 
 316:     case 'cypher':
 317:       return '\n---\nNext: To explore a result symbol in depth, run gitnexus-context "<name>"';
 318: 
 319:     case 'detect_changes':
 320:       return '\n---\nNext: Run gitnexus-context "<symbol>" on high-risk changed symbols to check their callers.';
 321: 
 322:     default:
 323:       return '';
 324:   }

 329: export async function evalServerCommand(options?: EvalServerOptions): Promise<void> {
 330:   const port = parseInt(options?.port || '4848');
 331:   const idleTimeoutSec = parseInt(options?.idleTimeout || '0');
 332: 
 333:   const backend = new LocalBackend();
 334:   const ok = await backend.init();
 335: 
 336:   if (!ok) {
 337:     // Operator-actionable but the server cannot start; warn-level so log
 338:     // aggregators don't trip error alerts on a configuration miss. Use
 339:     // cliWarn so the diagnostic reaches stderr synchronously before
 340:     // process.exit() — direct logger.warn would be lost to the buffered
 341:     // pino destination on hard exit (skips beforeExit flush).
 342:     cliWarn('GitNexus eval-server: No indexed repositories found. Run: gitnexus analyze');
 343:     process.exit(1);
 344:   }
 345: 
 346:   const repos = await backend.listRepos();
 347:   logger.info(
 348:     { repoCount: repos.length, repos: repos.map((r) => r.name) },
 349:     'GitNexus eval-server: repos loaded',
 350:   );
 351: 
 352:   let idleTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null;
 353: 
 354:   function resetIdleTimer() {
 355:     if (idleTimeoutSec <= 0) return;
 356:     if (idleTimer) clearTimeout(idleTimer);
 357:     idleTimer = setTimeout(async () => {
 358:       logger.info({ idleTimeoutSec }, 'GitNexus eval-server: idle timeout reached, shutting down');
 359:       await backend.disconnect();
 360:       process.exit(0);
 361:     }, idleTimeoutSec * 1000);
 362:   }
 363: 
 364:   const server = http.createServer(async (req, res) => {
 365:     resetIdleTimer();
 366: 
 367:     try {
 368:       // Health check
 369:       if (req.method === 'GET' && req.url === '/health') {
 370:         res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');
 371:         res.writeHead(200);
 372:         res.end(JSON.stringify({ status: 'ok', repos: repos.map((r) => r.name) }));
 373:         return;
 374:       }
 375: 
 376:       // Shutdown
 377:       if (req.method === 'POST' && req.url === '/shutdown') {
 378:         res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'application/json');
 379:         res.writeHead(200);
 380:         res.end(JSON.stringify({ status: 'shutting_down' }));
 381:         setTimeout(async () => {
 382:           await backend.disconnect();
 383:           server.close();
 384:           process.exit(0);
 385:         }, 100);
 386:         return;
 387:       }
 388: 
 389:       // Tool calls: POST /tool/:name
 390:       const toolMatch = req.url?.match(/^\/tool\/(\w+)$/);

 391:       if (req.method === 'POST' && toolMatch) {
 392:         const toolName = toolMatch[1];
 393: 
 394:         const body = await readBody(req);
 395:         let args: Record<string, any> = {};
 396:         if (body.trim()) {
 397:           try {
 398:             args = JSON.parse(body);
 399:           } catch {
 400:             res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/plain');
 401:             res.writeHead(400);
 402:             res.end('Error: Invalid JSON body');
 403:             return;
 404:           }
 405:         }
 406: 
 407:         // Call tool, format result as text, append next-step hint
 408:         const result = await backend.callTool(toolName, args);
 409:         const formatted = formatToolResult(toolName, result);
 410:         const hint = getNextStepHint(toolName);
 411: 
 412:         res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/plain');
 413:         res.writeHead(200);
 414:         res.end(formatted + hint);
 415:         return;
 416:       }
 417: 
 418:       // 404
 419:       res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/plain');
 420:       res.writeHead(404);
 421:       res.end('Not found. Use POST /tool/:name or GET /health');
 422:     } catch (err: any) {
 423:       res.setHeader('Content-Type', 'text/plain');
 424:       res.writeHead(500);
 425:       res.end(`Error: ${err.message || 'Internal error'}`);
 426:     }
 427:   });
 428: 
 429:   server.listen(port, '127.0.0.1', () => {
 430:     // Plain-text banner for the human watching stderr; structured record
 431:     // for log aggregation (split into two so the user sees a real banner
 432:     // not `{"level":30,"msg":"...","port":4747,"endpoints":[...]}`).
 433:     const bannerLines = [
 434:       `GitNexus eval-server: listening on http://127.0.0.1:${port}`,
 435:       `  POST /tool/query    — search execution flows`,
 436:       `  POST /tool/context  — 360-degree symbol view`,
 437:       `  POST /tool/impact   — blast radius analysis`,
 438:       `  POST /tool/cypher   — raw Cypher query`,
 439:       `  GET  /health        — health check`,
 440:       `  POST /shutdown      — graceful shutdown`,
 441:     ];
 442:     if (idleTimeoutSec > 0) {
 443:       bannerLines.push(`  Auto-shutdown after ${idleTimeoutSec}s idle`);
 444:     }
 445:     cliInfo(bannerLines.join('\n'), {
 446:       port,
 447:       host: '127.0.0.1',
 448:       idleTimeoutSec: idleTimeoutSec > 0 ? idleTimeoutSec : undefined,
 449:       endpoints: [
 450:         'POST /tool/query',
 451:         'POST /tool/context',
 452:         'POST /tool/impact',
 453:         'POST /tool/cypher',
 454:         'GET  /health',
 455:         'POST /shutdown',
 456:       ],
 457:     });
 458:     try {
 459:       // Use fd 1 directly — LadybugDB captures process.stdout (#324)
 460:       writeSync(1, `GITNEXUS_EVAL_SERVER_READY:${port}\n`);
 461:     } catch {
 462:       // stdout may not be available (e.g., broken pipe)
 463:     }
 464:   });
 465: 
 466:   resetIdleTimer();
 467: 
 468:   const shutdown = async () => {
 469:     logger.info('GitNexus eval-server: shutting down...');
 470:     await backend.disconnect();
 471:     server.close();
 472:     process.exit(0);
 473:   };
 474: 
 475:   process.on('SIGINT', shutdown);
 476:   process.on('SIGTERM', shutdown);
 477: }
 478: 
 479: export const MAX_BODY_SIZE = 1024 * 1024; // 1MB
 480: 
 481: function readBody(req: http.IncomingMessage): Promise<string> {
 482:   return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
 483:     const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
 484:     let totalSize = 0;
 485:     req.on('data', (chunk: Buffer) => {
 486:       totalSize += chunk.length;
 487:       if (totalSize > MAX_BODY_SIZE) {
 488:         req.destroy(new Error('Request body too large (max 1MB)'));
 489:         return;
 490:       }
 491:       chunks.push(chunk);
 492:     });
 493:     req.on('end', () => resolve(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('utf-8')));
 494:     req.on('error', reject);
 495:   });

 528:   async listRepos(): Promise<
 529:     Array<{
 530:       name: string;
 531:       path: string;
 532:       indexedAt: string;
 533:       lastCommit: string;
 534:       remoteUrl?: string;
 535:       stats?: any;
 536:       staleness?: { commitsBehind: number; hint?: string };
 537:       siblings?: Array<{ name: string; path: string; lastCommit: string }>;
 538:     }>
 539:   > {
 540:     await this.refreshRepos();
 541:     const handles = [...this.repos.values()];
 542: 
 543:     // Pre-group registered handles by `remoteUrl` so the sibling
 544:     // lookup is O(1) per handle. We reuse the in-memory `this.repos`
 545:     // (already populated by `refreshRepos`) instead of doing a fresh
 546:     // `readRegistry()` per entry — that would be N file reads for N
 547:     // registered repos.
 548:     const isWin = process.platform === 'win32';
 549:     const norm = (p: string) => (isWin ? path.resolve(p).toLowerCase() : path.resolve(p));
 550:     const byRemote = new Map<string, RepoHandle[]>();
 551:     for (const h of handles) {
 552:       if (!h.remoteUrl) continue;
 553:       const list = byRemote.get(h.remoteUrl) ?? [];
 554:       list.push(h);
 555:       byRemote.set(h.remoteUrl, list);
 556:     }
 557: 
 558:     // Check staleness for all repos in parallel instead of sequentially.
 559:     // Each check spawns an async `git rev-list` — with 200 repos the sync
 560:     // variant took ~50 s; parallel async brings it under a second (#1363).
 561:     const stalenessResults = await Promise.all(
 562:       handles.map((h) => checkStalenessAsync(h.repoPath, h.lastCommit)),
 563:     );
 564: 
 565:     return handles.map((h, i) => {
 566:       const stale = stalenessResults[i];
 567:       const selfNorm = norm(h.repoPath);
 568:       const siblings = h.remoteUrl
 569:         ? (byRemote.get(h.remoteUrl) ?? []).filter((e) => norm(e.repoPath) !== selfNorm)
 570:         : [];
 571:       return {
 572:         name: h.name,
 573:         path: h.repoPath,
 574:         indexedAt: h.indexedAt,
 575:         lastCommit: h.lastCommit,
 576:         remoteUrl: h.remoteUrl,
 577:         stats: h.stats,
 578:         staleness: stale.isStale
 579:           ? { commitsBehind: stale.commitsBehind, hint: stale.hint }
 580:           : undefined,
 581:         siblings:
 582:           siblings.length > 0
 583:             ? siblings.map((s) => ({
 584:                 name: s.name,
 585:                 path: s.repoPath,
 586:                 lastCommit: s.lastCommit,
 587:               }))
 588:             : undefined,
 589:       };
 590:     });
 591:   }
 592: 
 593:   /**
 594:    * Best-effort sibling-clone drift warning.
 595:    *
 596:    * When the resolved index has a `remoteUrl` recorded and the caller's
 597:    * `process.cwd()` is inside a *different* clone of the same repo, emit
 598:    * one stderr line per (repo, cwd) pair so the operator knows the
 599:    * graph may be stale relative to what's actually on disk under their
 600:    * cwd. Silent on path matches and on repos without a remote URL.
 601:    *
 602:    * Limitation: in MCP stdio server mode `process.cwd()` is the
 603:    * server's CWD at start time, *not* the agent client's CWD. The
 604:    * warning therefore only fires when the MCP server itself was
 605:    * launched from inside a sibling clone (typical for `npx gitnexus
 606:    * serve` from a polecat workspace). Surfacing the client's CWD
 607:    * would require a per-tool-call `cwd` parameter — out of scope for
 608:    * the current MCP contract.
 609:    *
 610:    * Pure side-effect (stderr); never affects the returned handle.
 611:    * After the first computation for a given (repo, cwd) pair the
 612:    * result is cached so subsequent `resolveRepo()` calls don't
 613:    * re-shell-out to git.
 614:    */
 615:   private async maybeWarnSiblingDrift(handle: RepoHandle): Promise<void> {
 616:     if (!handle.remoteUrl) return;
 617:     let cwd: string;
 618:     try {
 619:       cwd = process.cwd();
 620:     } catch {
 621:       return;
 622:     }
 623:     // Early-exit cache: keyed on (repo, cwd) BEFORE any git shellout.
 624:     // After the first call for a given cwd, this short-circuits the
 625:     // up-to-four `execSync`/`execFileSync` calls inside `checkCwdMatch`
 626:     // — important for MCP-server mode where `process.cwd()` is constant
 627:     // and `resolveRepo` runs on every tool call.
 628:     const cacheKey = `${handle.id}|${cwd}`;
 629:     if (this.warnedSiblingDrift.has(cacheKey)) return;
 630: 
 631:     const match = await checkCwdMatch(cwd);
 632:     if (
 633:       match.match !== 'sibling-by-remote' ||
 634:       !match.entry ||
 635:       !match.cwdGitRoot ||
 636:       match.entry.path !== handle.repoPath ||
 637:       !match.hint
 638:     ) {
 639:       // Cache "nothing to warn about" outcomes too — `checkCwdMatch`
 640:       // is deterministic for a fixed (registry, cwd) pair, so re-running
 641:       // it yields nothing new.
 642:       this.warnedSiblingDrift.add(cacheKey);
 643:       return;
 644:     }
 645: 
 646:     this.warnedSiblingDrift.add(cacheKey);
 647:     logger.error(`GitNexus: ${match.hint}`);
 648:   }

 652:   async callTool(method: string, params: any): Promise<any> {
 653:     if (method === 'list_repos') {
 654:       return this.listRepos();
 655:     }
 656: 
 657:     if (method.startsWith('group_')) {
 658:       return this.handleGroupTool(method, params || {});
 659:     }
 660: 
 661:     const p = params && typeof params === 'object' ? (params as Record<string, unknown>) : {};
 662:     if (
 663:       (method === 'impact' || method === 'query' || method === 'context') &&
 664:       typeof p.repo === 'string' &&
 665:       p.repo.startsWith('@')
 666:     ) {
 667:       return this.callToolAtGroupRepo(method, p);
 668:     }
 669: 
 670:     // Resolve repo from optional param (re-reads registry on miss)
 671:     const repo = await this.resolveRepo((params as { repo?: string } | undefined)?.repo);
 672: 
 673:     switch (method) {
 674:       case 'query':
 675:         return this.query(repo, params);
 676:       case 'cypher': {
 677:         const raw = await this.cypher(repo, params);
 678:         return this.formatCypherAsMarkdown(raw);
 679:       }
 680:       case 'context':
 681:         return this.context(repo, params);
 682:       case 'impact':
 683:         return this.impact(repo, params);
 684:       case 'detect_changes':
 685:         return this.detectChanges(repo, params);
 686:       case 'rename':
 687:         return this.rename(repo, params);
 688:       // Legacy aliases for backwards compatibility
 689:       case 'search':
 690:         return this.query(repo, params);
 691:       case 'explore':
 692:         return this.context(repo, { name: params?.name, ...params });
 693:       case 'overview':
 694:         return this.overview(repo, params);
 695:       case 'route_map':
 696:         return this.routeMap(repo, params);
 697:       case 'shape_check':
 698:         return this.shapeCheck(repo, params);
 699:       case 'tool_map':
 700:         return this.toolMap(repo, params);
 701:       case 'api_impact':
 702:         return this.apiImpact(repo, params);
 703:       default:
 704:         throw new Error(`Unknown tool: ${method}`);
 705:     }

 718:   private async query(
 719:     repo: RepoHandle,
 720:     params: {
 721:       query: string;
 722:       task_context?: string;
 723:       goal?: string;
 724:       limit?: number;
 725:       max_symbols?: number;
 726:       include_content?: boolean;
 727:     },
 728:   ): Promise<any> {
 729:     if (!params.query?.trim()) {
 730:       return { error: 'query parameter is required and cannot be empty.' };
 731:     }
 732: 
 733:     await this.ensureInitialized(repo.id);
 734: 
 735:     const processLimit = params.limit || 5;
 736:     const maxSymbolsPerProcess = params.max_symbols || 10;
 737:     const includeContent = params.include_content ?? false;
 738:     const searchQuery = params.query.trim();
 739: 
 740:     // Per-phase timing instrumentation (#553). Records wall time for each
 741:     // observable sub-step of the search pipeline so production latency can
 742:     // be aggregated offline for Pareto analysis and bottleneck detection.
 743:     // Overhead is <0.1 ms per phase; the timer is passive and never alters
 744:     // query behaviour.
 745:     const timer = new PhaseTimer();
 746:     const wallStart = performance.now();
 747: 
 748:     // Step 1: Run hybrid search to get matching symbols. BM25 and vector
 749:     // search run concurrently via Promise.all — use `timer.time()` for
 750:     // each so both get independent wall-time records without fighting
 751:     // over a single `current` phase slot.
 752:     const searchLimit = processLimit * maxSymbolsPerProcess; // fetch enough raw results
 753:     const [bm25SearchResult, semanticResults] = await Promise.all([
 754:       timer.time('bm25', this.bm25Search(repo, searchQuery, searchLimit)),
 755:       timer.time('vector', this.semanticSearch(repo, searchQuery, searchLimit)),
 756:     ]);
 757: 
 758:     const bm25Results = bm25SearchResult.results;
 759:     const ftsUsed = bm25SearchResult.ftsUsed;
 760: 
 761:     // Merge via reciprocal rank fusion
 762:     timer.start('merge');
 763:     const scoreMap = new Map<string, { score: number; data: any }>();
 764: 
 765:     for (let i = 0; i < bm25Results.length; i++) {
 766:       const result = bm25Results[i];
 767:       const key = result.nodeId || result.filePath;
 768:       const rrfScore = 1 / (60 + i);
 769:       const existing = scoreMap.get(key);
 770:       if (existing) {
 771:         existing.score += rrfScore;
 772:       } else {
 773:         scoreMap.set(key, { score: rrfScore, data: result });
 774:       }
 775:     }
 776: 
 777:     for (let i = 0; i < semanticResults.length; i++) {
 778:       const result = semanticResults[i];
 779:       const key = result.nodeId || result.filePath;
 780:       const rrfScore = 1 / (60 + i);
 781:       const existing = scoreMap.get(key);
 782:       if (existing) {
 783:         existing.score += rrfScore;
 784:       } else {
 785:         scoreMap.set(key, { score: rrfScore, data: result });
 786:       }
 787:     }
 788: 
 789:     const merged = Array.from(scoreMap.entries())
 790:       .sort((a, b) => b[1].score - a[1].score)
 791:       .slice(0, searchLimit);
 792:     timer.stop(); // merge
 793: 
 794:     // Step 2: For each match with a nodeId, trace to process(es)
 795:     timer.start('symbol_lookup');
 796:     const processMap = new Map<
 797:       string,
 798:       {
 799:         id: string;
 800:         label: string;
 801:         heuristicLabel: string;
 802:         processType: string;
 803:         stepCount: number;
 804:         totalScore: number;
 805:         cohesionBoost: number;
 806:         symbols: any[];
 807:       }
 808:     >();
 809:     const definitions: any[] = []; // standalone symbols not in any process
 810: 
 811:     for (const [_, item] of merged) {
 812:       const sym = item.data;
 813:       if (!sym.nodeId) {
 814:         // File-level results go to definitions
 815:         definitions.push({
 816:           name: sym.name,
 817:           type: sym.type || 'File',
 818:           filePath: sym.filePath,
 819:         });
 820:         continue;
 821:       }
 822: 
 823:       // Find processes this symbol participates in
 824:       let processRows: any[] = [];
 825:       try {
 826:         processRows = await executeParameterized(
 827:           repo.id,
 828:           `
 829:           MATCH (n {id: $nodeId})-[r:CodeRelation {type: 'STEP_IN_PROCESS'}]->(p:Process)
 830:           RETURN p.id AS pid, p.label AS label, p.heuristicLabel AS heuristicLabel, p.processType AS processType, p.stepCount AS stepCount, r.step AS step
 831:         `,
 832:           { nodeId: sym.nodeId },
 833:         );
 834:       } catch (e) {
 835:         logQueryError('query:process-lookup', e);
 836:       }
 837: 
 838:       // Get cluster membership + cohesion (cohesion used as internal ranking signal)
 839:       let cohesion = 0;
 840:       let module: string | undefined;
 841:       try {
 842:         const cohesionRows = await executeParameterized(
 843:           repo.id,
 844:           `
 845:           MATCH (n {id: $nodeId})-[:CodeRelation {type: 'MEMBER_OF'}]->(c:Community)
 846:           RETURN c.cohesion AS cohesion, c.heuristicLabel AS module
 847:           LIMIT 1
 848:         `,
 849:           { nodeId: sym.nodeId },
 850:         );
 851:         if (cohesionRows.length > 0) {
 852:           cohesion = (cohesionRows[0].cohesion ?? cohesionRows[0][0]) || 0;
 853:           module = cohesionRows[0].module ?? cohesionRows[0][1];
 854:         }
 855:       } catch (e) {
 856:         logQueryError('query:cluster-info', e);
 857:       }
 858: 
 859:       // Optionally fetch content
 860:       let content: string | undefined;

 861:       if (includeContent) {
 862:         try {
 863:           const contentRows = await executeParameterized(
 864:             repo.id,
 865:             `
 866:             MATCH (n {id: $nodeId})
 867:             RETURN n.content AS content
 868:           `,
 869:             { nodeId: sym.nodeId },
 870:           );
 871:           if (contentRows.length > 0) {
 872:             content = contentRows[0].content ?? contentRows[0][0];
 873:           }
 874:         } catch (e) {
 875:           logQueryError('query:content-fetch', e);
 876:         }
 877:       }
 878: 
 879:       const symbolEntry = {
 880:         id: sym.nodeId,
 881:         name: sym.name,
 882:         type: sym.type,
 883:         filePath: sym.filePath,
 884:         startLine: sym.startLine,
 885:         endLine: sym.endLine,
 886:         ...(module ? { module } : {}),
 887:         ...(includeContent && content ? { content } : {}),
 888:       };
 889: 
 890:       if (processRows.length === 0) {
 891:         // Symbol not in any process — goes to definitions
 892:         definitions.push(symbolEntry);

1241:   /**
1242:    * Format raw Cypher result rows as a markdown table for LLM readability.
1243:    * Falls back to raw result if rows aren't tabular objects.
1244:    */
1245:   private formatCypherAsMarkdown(result: any): any {
1246:     if (!Array.isArray(result) || result.length === 0) return result;
1247: 
1248:     const firstRow = result[0];
1249:     if (typeof firstRow !== 'object' || firstRow === null) return result;
1250: 
1251:     const keys = Object.keys(firstRow);
1252:     if (keys.length === 0) return result;
1253: 
1254:     const header = '| ' + keys.join(' | ') + ' |';
1255:     const separator = '| ' + keys.map(() => '---').join(' | ') + ' |';
1256:     const dataRows = result.map(
1257:       (row: any) =>
1258:         '| ' +
1259:         keys
1260:           .map((k) => {
1261:             const v = row[k];
1262:             if (v === null || v === undefined) return '';
1263:             if (typeof v === 'object') return JSON.stringify(v);
1264:             return String(v);
1265:           })
1266:           .join(' | ') +
1267:         ' |',
1268:     );
1269: 
1270:     return {
1271:       markdown: [header, separator, ...dataRows].join('\n'),
1272:       row_count: result.length,
1273:     };

1276:   /**
1277:    * Aggregate same-named clusters: group by heuristicLabel, sum symbols,
1278:    * weighted-average cohesion, filter out tiny clusters (<5 symbols).
1279:    * Raw communities stay intact in LadybugDB for Cypher queries.
1280:    */
1281:   private aggregateClusters(clusters: any[]): any[] {
1282:     const groups = new Map<
1283:       string,
1284:       { ids: string[]; totalSymbols: number; weightedCohesion: number; largest: any }
1285:     >();
1286: 
1287:     for (const c of clusters) {
1288:       const label = c.heuristicLabel || c.label || 'Unknown';
1289:       const symbols = c.symbolCount || 0;
1290:       const cohesion = c.cohesion || 0;
1291:       const existing = groups.get(label);
1292: 
1293:       if (!existing) {
1294:         groups.set(label, {
1295:           ids: [c.id],
1296:           totalSymbols: symbols,
1297:           weightedCohesion: cohesion * symbols,
1298:           largest: c,
1299:         });
1300:       } else {
1301:         existing.ids.push(c.id);
1302:         existing.totalSymbols += symbols;
1303:         existing.weightedCohesion += cohesion * symbols;
1304:         if (symbols > (existing.largest.symbolCount || 0)) {
1305:           existing.largest = c;
1306:         }
1307:       }
1308:     }
1309: 
1310:     return Array.from(groups.entries())
1311:       .map(([label, g]) => ({
1312:         id: g.largest.id,
1313:         label,
1314:         heuristicLabel: label,
1315:         symbolCount: g.totalSymbols,
1316:         cohesion: g.totalSymbols > 0 ? g.weightedCohesion / g.totalSymbols : 0,
1317:         subCommunities: g.ids.length,
1318:       }))
1319:       .filter((c) => c.symbolCount >= 5)
1320:       .sort((a, b) => b.symbolCount - a.symbolCount);
