1706:   private async _contextImpl(
1707:     repo: RepoHandle,
1708:     params: {
1709:       name?: string;
1710:       uid?: string;
1711:       file_path?: string;
1712:       kind?: string;
1713:       include_content?: boolean;
1714:     },
1715:   ): Promise<any> {
1716:     await this.ensureInitialized(repo.id);
1717: 
1718:     const { name, uid, file_path, kind, include_content } = params;
1719: 
1720:     if (!name && !uid) {
1721:       return { error: 'Either "name" or "uid" parameter is required.' };
1722:     }
1723: 
1724:     const outcome = await this.resolveSymbolCandidates(
1725:       repo,
1726:       { uid, name, include_content },
1727:       { file_path, kind },
1728:     );
1729: 
1730:     if (outcome.kind === 'not_found') {
1731:       return { error: `Symbol '${name || uid}' not found` };
1732:     }
1733: 
1734:     if (outcome.kind === 'ambiguous') {
1735:       return {
1736:         status: 'ambiguous',
1737:         message: `Found ${outcome.candidates.length} symbols matching '${name}'. Use uid, file_path, or kind to disambiguate.`,
1738:         candidates: outcome.candidates.map((c) => ({
1739:           uid: c.id,
1740:           name: c.name,
1741:           kind: c.type,
1742:           filePath: c.filePath,
1743:           line: c.startLine,
1744:           score: Number(c.score.toFixed(2)),
1745:         })),
1746:       };
1747:     }
1748: 
1749:     // Step 3: Build full context
1750:     const sym = outcome.symbol;
1751:     const resolvedLabel = outcome.resolvedLabel;
1752:     const symId = sym.id;
1753: 
1754:     // Categorized incoming refs
1755:     const incomingRows = await executeParameterized(
1756:       repo.id,
1757:       `
1758:       MATCH (caller)-[r:CodeRelation]->(n {id: $symId})
1759:       WHERE r.type IN ['CALLS', 'IMPORTS', 'EXTENDS', 'IMPLEMENTS', 'HAS_METHOD', 'HAS_PROPERTY', 'METHOD_OVERRIDES', 'OVERRIDES', 'METHOD_IMPLEMENTS', 'ACCESSES']
1760:       RETURN r.type AS relType, caller.id AS uid, caller.name AS name, caller.filePath AS filePath, labels(caller)[0] AS kind
1761:       LIMIT 30
1762:     `,
1763:       { symId },
1764:     );
1765: 
1766:     // Fix #480: Class/Interface nodes have no direct CALLS/IMPORTS edges —
1767:     // those point to Constructor and File nodes respectively. Fetch those
1768:     // extra incoming refs and merge them in so context() shows real callers.
1769:     //
1770:     // Determine if this is a Class/Interface node. If resolvedLabel was set
1771:     // during disambiguation (Step 2), use it directly — no extra round-trip.
1772:     // Otherwise fall back to a single label check only when the type field is
1773:     // empty (LadybugDB labels(n)[0] limitation).
1774:     const symRawType = sym.type || sym[2] || '';
1775:     let isClassLike = resolvedLabel === 'Class' || resolvedLabel === 'Interface';
1776:     if (!isClassLike && symRawType === '') {
1777:       try {
1778:         // Single UNION query instead of two serial round-trips.
1779:         const typeCheck = await executeParameterized(
1780:           repo.id,
1781:           `
1782:           MATCH (n:Class) WHERE n.id = $symId RETURN 'Class' AS label LIMIT 1
1783:           UNION ALL
1784:           MATCH (n:Interface) WHERE n.id = $symId RETURN 'Interface' AS label LIMIT 1
1785:         `,
1786:           { symId },
1787:         );
1788:         isClassLike = typeCheck.length > 0;
1789:       } catch {
1790:         /* not a Class/Interface node */
1791:       }
1792:     } else if (!isClassLike) {
1793:       isClassLike = symRawType === 'Class' || symRawType === 'Interface';
1794:     }
1795: 
1796:     if (isClassLike) {
1797:       try {
1798:         // Run both incoming-ref queries in parallel — they are independent.
1799:         const [ctorIncoming, fileIncoming] = await Promise.all([
1800:           executeParameterized(
1801:             repo.id,
1802:             `
1803:             MATCH (n)-[hm:CodeRelation]->(ctor:Constructor)
1804:             WHERE n.id = $symId AND hm.type = 'HAS_METHOD'
1805:             MATCH (caller)-[r:CodeRelation]->(ctor)
1806:             WHERE r.type IN ['CALLS', 'IMPORTS', 'EXTENDS', 'IMPLEMENTS', 'ACCESSES']
1807:             RETURN r.type AS relType, caller.id AS uid, caller.name AS name, caller.filePath AS filePath, labels(caller)[0] AS kind
1808:             LIMIT 30
1809:           `,
1810:             { symId },
1811:           ),
1812:           executeParameterized(
1813:             repo.id,
1814:             `
1815:             MATCH (f:File)-[rel:CodeRelation]->(n)
1816:             WHERE n.id = $symId AND rel.type = 'DEFINES'
1817:             MATCH (caller)-[r:CodeRelation]->(f)
1818:             WHERE r.type IN ['CALLS', 'IMPORTS']
1819:             RETURN r.type AS relType, caller.id AS uid, caller.name AS name, caller.filePath AS filePath, labels(caller)[0] AS kind
1820:             LIMIT 30
1821:           `,
1822:             { symId },
1823:           ),
1824:         ]);
1825: 
1826:         // Deduplicate by (relType, uid) — a caller can have multiple relation
1827:         // types to the same target (e.g. both IMPORTS and CALLS), and each
1828:         // must be preserved so every category appears in the output.
1829:         const seenKeys = new Set(
1830:           incomingRows.map((r: any) => `${r.relType || r[0]}:${r.uid || r[1]}`),
1831:         );
1832:         for (const r of [...ctorIncoming, ...fileIncoming]) {
1833:           const key = `${r.relType || r[0]}:${r.uid || r[1]}`;
1834:           if (!seenKeys.has(key)) {
1835:             seenKeys.add(key);

1836:             incomingRows.push(r);
1837:           }
1838:         }
1839:       } catch (e) {
1840:         logQueryError('context:class-incoming-expansion', e);
1841:       }
1842:     }
1843: 
1844:     // Categorized outgoing refs
1845:     const outgoingRows = await executeParameterized(
1846:       repo.id,
1847:       `
1848:       MATCH (n {id: $symId})-[r:CodeRelation]->(target)
1849:       WHERE r.type IN ['CALLS', 'IMPORTS', 'EXTENDS', 'IMPLEMENTS', 'HAS_METHOD', 'HAS_PROPERTY', 'METHOD_OVERRIDES', 'OVERRIDES', 'METHOD_IMPLEMENTS', 'ACCESSES']
1850:       RETURN r.type AS relType, target.id AS uid, target.name AS name, target.filePath AS filePath, labels(target)[0] AS kind
1851:       LIMIT 30
1852:     `,
1853:       { symId },
1854:     );
1855: 
1856:     // Process participation
1857:     let processRows: any[] = [];
1858:     try {
1859:       processRows = await executeParameterized(
1860:         repo.id,
1861:         `
1862:         MATCH (n {id: $symId})-[r:CodeRelation {type: 'STEP_IN_PROCESS'}]->(p:Process)
1863:         RETURN p.id AS pid, p.heuristicLabel AS label, r.step AS step, p.stepCount AS stepCount
1864:       `,
1865:         { symId },
1866:       );
1867:     } catch (e) {
1868:       logQueryError('context:process-participation', e);
1869:     }
1870: 
1871:     // Helper to categorize refs
1872:     const categorize = (rows: any[]) => {
1873:       const cats: Record<string, any[]> = {};
1874:       for (const row of rows) {
1875:         const relType = (row.relType || row[0] || '').toLowerCase();
1876:         const entry = {
1877:           uid: row.uid || row[1],
1878:           name: row.name || row[2],
1879:           filePath: row.filePath || row[3],
1880:           kind: row.kind || row[4],
1881:         };
1882:         if (!cats[relType]) cats[relType] = [];
1883:         cats[relType].push(entry);
1884:       }
1885:       return cats;
1886:     };
1887: 
1888:     // Method/Function/Constructor enrichment: fetch method-specific properties
1889:     const symKind = isClassLike ? resolvedLabel || 'Class' : sym.type || sym[2];
1890:     const isMethodLike =
1891:       symKind === 'Method' || symKind === 'Function' || symKind === 'Constructor';
1892:     let methodMetadata: Record<string, unknown> | undefined;
1893:     if (isMethodLike) {
1894:       try {
1895:         const metaRows = await executeParameterized(
1896:           repo.id,
1897:           `
1898:           MATCH (n {id: $symId})
1899:           RETURN n.visibility AS visibility, n.isStatic AS isStatic, n.isAbstract AS isAbstract,
1900:                  n.isFinal AS isFinal, n.isVirtual AS isVirtual, n.isOverride AS isOverride,
1901:                  n.isAsync AS isAsync, n.isPartial AS isPartial, n.returnType AS returnType,
1902:                  n.parameterCount AS parameterCount, n.isVariadic AS isVariadic,
1903:                  n.requiredParameterCount AS requiredParameterCount,
1904:                  n.parameterTypes AS parameterTypes, n.annotations AS annotations

1913:           for (const key of Object.keys(row)) {

1916:           }
1917:           if (Object.keys(meta).length > 0) methodMetadata = meta;

1919:       } catch {

1923: 
1924:     return {

2375:         '.',
2376:       ];
2377:       const output = execFileSync('rg', rgArgs, {
2378:         cwd: repo.repoPath,
2379:         encoding: 'utf-8',
2380:         timeout: 5000,
2381:         // Avoid ENOBUFS on large repos: rg -l can list many files.
2382:         maxBuffer: 256 * 1024 * 1024,
2383:       });
2384:       const files = output
2385:         .trim()
2386:         .split('\n')
2387:         .filter((f) => f.length > 0);
2388: 
2389:       for (const file of files) {
2390:         const normalizedFile = file.replace(/\\/g, '/').replace(/^\.\//, '');
2391:         if (graphFiles.has(normalizedFile)) continue; // already covered by graph
2392: 
2393:         try {
2394:           const content = await fs.readFile(assertSafePath(normalizedFile), 'utf-8');
2395:           const lines = content.split('\n');
2396:           const regex = new RegExp(`\\b${oldName.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&')}\\b`, 'g');
2397:           for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i++) {
2398:             regex.lastIndex = 0;
2399:             if (regex.test(lines[i])) {
2400:               regex.lastIndex = 0;
2401:               addEdit(
2402:                 normalizedFile,
2403:                 i + 1,
2404:                 lines[i].trim(),
2405:                 lines[i].replace(regex, new_name).trim(),
2406:                 'text_search',
2407:               );
2408:               astSearchEdits++;
2409:             }
2410:           }
2411:         } catch (e) {
2412:           logQueryError('rename:text-search-read', e);
2413:         }
2414:       }
2415:     } catch (e) {
2416:       logQueryError('rename:ripgrep', e);
2417:     }
2418: 
2419:     // Step 4: Apply or preview
2420:     const allChanges = Array.from(changes.values());
2421:     const totalEdits = allChanges.reduce((sum, c) => sum + c.edits.length, 0);
2422: 
2423:     if (!dry_run) {
2424:       // Apply edits to files
2425:       for (const change of allChanges) {
2426:         try {
2427:           const fullPath = assertSafePath(change.file_path);
2428:           let content = await fs.readFile(fullPath, 'utf-8');
2429:           const regex = new RegExp(`\\b${oldName.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&')}\\b`, 'g');
2430:           content = content.replace(regex, new_name);
2431:           await fs.writeFile(fullPath, content, 'utf-8');
2432:         } catch (e) {
2433:           logQueryError('rename:apply-edit', e);
2434:         }
2435:       }
2436:     }
2437: 
2438:     return {
2439:       status: 'success',
2440:       old_name: oldName,
2441:       new_name,
2442:       files_affected: allChanges.length,
2443:       total_edits: totalEdits,
2444:       graph_edits: graphEdits,
2445:       text_search_edits: astSearchEdits,
2446:       changes: allChanges,
2447:       applied: !dry_run,
2448:     };
2449:   }
2450: 

2451:   private async impact(
2452:     repo: RepoHandle,
2453:     params: {
2454:       target: string;
2455:       target_uid?: string;
2456:       file_path?: string;
2457:       kind?: string;
2458:       direction: 'upstream' | 'downstream';
2459:       maxDepth?: number;
2460:       relationTypes?: string[];
2461:       includeTests?: boolean;
2462:       minConfidence?: number;
2463:     },
2464:   ): Promise<any> {
2465:     try {
2466:       return await this._impactImpl(repo, params);
2467:     } catch (err: any) {
2468:       // Return structured error instead of crashing (#321)
2469:       return {
2470:         error: (err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)) || 'Impact analysis failed',
2471:         target: { name: params.target },
2472:         direction: params.direction,
2473:         impactedCount: 0,
2474:         risk: 'UNKNOWN',
2475:         suggestion: 'The graph query failed — try gitnexus context <symbol> as a fallback',
2476:         ...(isWalCorruptionError(err) ? { recoverySuggestion: WAL_RECOVERY_SUGGESTION } : {}),
2477:       };
2478:     }
2479:   }
2480: 
2481:   private async _impactImpl(
2482:     repo: RepoHandle,
2483:     params: {
2484:       target: string;
2485:       target_uid?: string;
2486:       file_path?: string;
2487:       kind?: string;
2488:       direction: 'upstream' | 'downstream';
2489:       maxDepth?: number;
2490:       relationTypes?: string[];
2491:       includeTests?: boolean;
2492:       minConfidence?: number;
2493:     },
2494:   ): Promise<any> {
2495:     await this.ensureInitialized(repo.id);
2496: 
2497:     const { target, direction } = params;
2498:     const maxDepth = params.maxDepth || 3;
2499:     // Map legacy relation type names before filtering (backward compat for OVERRIDES → METHOD_OVERRIDES)
2500:     const mappedRelTypes = params.relationTypes?.flatMap((t: string) =>
2501:       t === 'OVERRIDES' ? ['OVERRIDES', 'METHOD_OVERRIDES'] : [t],
2502:     );
2503:     const rawRelTypes =
2504:       mappedRelTypes && mappedRelTypes.length > 0
2505:         ? mappedRelTypes.filter((t: string) => VALID_RELATION_TYPES.has(t))
2506:         : [
2507:             'CALLS',
2508:             'IMPORTS',
2509:             'EXTENDS',
2510:             'IMPLEMENTS',
2511:             'METHOD_OVERRIDES',
2512:             'OVERRIDES',
2513:             'METHOD_IMPLEMENTS',
2514:           ];
2515:     const relationTypes =
2516:       rawRelTypes.length > 0
2517:         ? rawRelTypes
2518:         : [
2519:             'CALLS',
2520:             'IMPORTS',
2521:             'EXTENDS',
2522:             'IMPLEMENTS',
2523:             'METHOD_OVERRIDES',
2524:             'OVERRIDES',
2525:             'METHOD_IMPLEMENTS',
2526:           ];
2527:     const includeTests = params.includeTests ?? false;
2528:     const minConfidence = params.minConfidence ?? 0;
2529: 
2530:     // Resolve target via the shared symbol resolver. When the caller passes
2531:     // target_uid we skip the name lookup entirely (zero-ambiguity). Otherwise
2532:     // we rank candidates (#470) and either proceed with a confident single
2533:     // match, or return a structured ambiguous response instead of silently
2534:     // picking the wrong symbol.
2535:     //
2536:     // The resolver preserves the #480 Class/Constructor preference heuristic:
2537:     // when a Class and its Constructor share name + filePath, the Class is
2538:     // selected silently.
2539:     const outcome = await this.resolveSymbolCandidates(
2540:       repo,
2541:       { uid: params.target_uid, name: target },
2542:       { file_path: params.file_path, kind: params.kind },
2543:     );
2544: 
2545:     if (outcome.kind === 'not_found') {
2546:       const missing = params.target_uid ?? target;
2547:       return {
2548:         error: `Target '${missing}' not found`,
2549:         target: { name: target },
2550:         direction,
2551:         impactedCount: 0,
2552:         risk: 'UNKNOWN',
2553:       };
2554:     }
2555: 
2556:     if (outcome.kind === 'ambiguous') {
2557:       return {
2558:         status: 'ambiguous',
2559:         message: `Found ${outcome.candidates.length} symbols matching '${target}'. Use target_uid, file_path, or kind to disambiguate.`,
2560:         target: { name: target },
2561:         direction,
2562:         impactedCount: 0,
2563:         risk: 'UNKNOWN',
2564:         candidates: outcome.candidates.map((c) => ({
2565:           uid: c.id,
2566:           name: c.name,
2567:           kind: c.type,
2568:           filePath: c.filePath,
2569:           line: c.startLine,
2570:           score: Number(c.score.toFixed(2)),
2571:         })),
2572:       };
2573:     }
2574: 
2575:     const sym = {
2576:       id: outcome.symbol.id,
2577:       name: outcome.symbol.name,
2578:       filePath: outcome.symbol.filePath,
2579:     };
2580:     const symType = outcome.resolvedLabel || outcome.symbol.type || '';
2581: 
2582:     return this._runImpactBFS(repo, sym, symType, direction, {
2583:       maxDepth,
2584:       relationTypes,
2585:       includeTests,
2586:       minConfidence,
2587:     });
2588:   }
2589: 
2590:   /**
2591:    * Shared BFS traversal for impact analysis (name-resolved or UID-resolved symbol).
2592:    */
2593:   private async _runImpactBFS(
2594:     repo: RepoHandle,
2595:     sym: any,
2596:     symType: string,
2597:     direction: 'upstream' | 'downstream',
2598:     opts: {
2599:       maxDepth: number;
2600:       relationTypes: string[];
2601:       includeTests: boolean;
2602:       minConfidence: number;
2603:     },
2604:   ): Promise<any> {
2605:     const { maxDepth, relationTypes, includeTests, minConfidence } = opts;

2606:     const relTypeFilter = relationTypes.map((t) => `'${t}'`).join(', ');
2607:     const confidenceFilter = minConfidence > 0 ? ` AND r.confidence >= ${minConfidence}` : '';
2608: 
2609:     const symId = sym.id || sym[0];
2610: 
2611:     const impacted: any[] = [];
2612:     const visited = new Set<string>([symId]);
2613:     let frontier = [symId];
2614:     let traversalComplete = true;
2615: 
2616:     // Fix #480: For Java (and other JVM) Class/Interface nodes, CALLS edges
2617:     // point to Constructor nodes and IMPORTS edges point to File nodes — not
2618:     // the Class/Interface itself. Seed the frontier with the Constructor(s)
2619:     // and owning File so the BFS traversal finds those edges naturally.
2620:     // The owning File is kept only as an internal seed (frontier/visited) and
2621:     // is NOT added to impacted — it is the definition container, not an
2622:     // upstream dependent. The BFS will discover IMPORTS edges on it naturally.
2623:     if (symType === 'Class' || symType === 'Interface') {
2624:       try {
2625:         // Run both seed queries in parallel — they are independent.
2626:         const [ctorRows, fileRows] = await Promise.all([
2627:           executeParameterized(
2628:             repo.id,
2629:             `
2630:             MATCH (n)-[hm:CodeRelation]->(c:Constructor)
2631:             WHERE n.id = $symId AND hm.type = 'HAS_METHOD'
2632:             RETURN c.id AS id, c.name AS name, labels(c)[0] AS type, c.filePath AS filePath
2633:           `,
2634:             { symId },
2635:           ),
2636:           // Restrict to DEFINES edges only — other File->Class edge types (if
2637:           // any) should not be treated as the owning file relationship.
2638:           executeParameterized(
2639:             repo.id,
2640:             `
2641:             MATCH (f:File)-[rel:CodeRelation]->(n)
2642:             WHERE n.id = $symId AND rel.type = 'DEFINES'
2643:             RETURN f.id AS id, f.name AS name, labels(f)[0] AS type, f.filePath AS filePath
2644:           `,
2645:             { symId },
2646:           ),
2647:         ]);
2648: 
2649:         for (const r of ctorRows) {
2650:           const rid = r.id || r[0];
2651:           if (rid && !visited.has(rid)) {
2652:             visited.add(rid);
2653:             frontier.push(rid);
2654:           }
2655:         }
2656:         for (const r of fileRows) {
2657:           const rid = r.id || r[0];
2658:           if (rid && !visited.has(rid)) {
2659:             visited.add(rid);
2660:             frontier.push(rid);
2661:           }
2662:         }
2663:       } catch (e) {
2664:         logQueryError('impact:class-node-expansion', e);
2665:       }
2666:     }
2667: 
2668:     for (let depth = 1; depth <= maxDepth && frontier.length > 0; depth++) {
2669:       const nextFrontier: string[] = [];
2670: 
2671:       // Batch frontier nodes into a single Cypher query per depth level
2672:       const idList = frontier.map((id) => `'${id.replace(/'/g, "''")}'`).join(', ');
2673:       const query =
2674:         direction === 'upstream'
2675:           ? `MATCH (caller)-[r:CodeRelation]->(n) WHERE n.id IN [${idList}] AND r.type IN [${relTypeFilter}]${confidenceFilter} RETURN n.id AS sourceId, caller.id AS id, caller.name AS name, labels(caller)[0] AS type, caller.filePath AS filePath, r.type AS relType, r.confidence AS confidence`
2676:           : `MATCH (n)-[r:CodeRelation]->(callee) WHERE n.id IN [${idList}] AND r.type IN [${relTypeFilter}]${confidenceFilter} RETURN n.id AS sourceId, callee.id AS id, callee.name AS name, labels(callee)[0] AS type, callee.filePath AS filePath, r.type AS relType, r.confidence AS confidence`;
2677: 
2678:       try {
2679:         const related = await executeQuery(repo.id, query);
2680: 
2681:         for (const rel of related) {
2682:           const relId = rel.id || rel[1];
2683:           const filePath = rel.filePath || rel[4] || '';
2684: 
2685:           if (!includeTests && isTestFilePath(filePath)) continue;
2686: 
2687:           if (!visited.has(relId)) {
2688:             visited.add(relId);
2689:             nextFrontier.push(relId);
2690:             const storedConfidence = rel.confidence ?? rel[6];
2691:             const relationType = rel.relType || rel[5];
2692:             // Prefer the stored confidence from the graph (set at analysis time);
2693:             // fall back to the per-type floor for edges without a stored value.
2694:             const effectiveConfidence =
2695:               typeof storedConfidence === 'number' && storedConfidence > 0
2696:                 ? storedConfidence
2697:                 : confidenceForRelType(relationType);
2698:             impacted.push({
2699:               depth,
2700:               id: relId,
2701:               name: rel.name || rel[2],
2702:               type: rel.type || rel[3],
2703:               filePath,
2704:               relationType,
2705:               confidence: effectiveConfidence,
2706:             });
2707:           }
2708:         }
2709:       } catch (e) {
2710:         logQueryError('impact:depth-traversal', e);
2711:         // Break out of depth loop on query failure but return partial results
2712:         // collected so far, rather than silently swallowing the error (#321)
2713:         traversalComplete = false;
2714:         break;
2715:       }
2716: 
2717:       frontier = nextFrontier;
2718:     }
2719: 
2720:     const grouped: Record<number, any[]> = {};
2721:     for (const item of impacted) {
2722:       if (!grouped[item.depth]) grouped[item.depth] = [];
2723:       grouped[item.depth].push(item);
2724:     }
2725: 
2726:     // ── Enrichment: affected processes, modules, risk ──────────────
2727:     const directCount = (grouped[1] || []).length;
2728:     let affectedProcesses: any[] = [];
2729:     let affectedModules: any[] = [];
2730: 
2731:     if (impacted.length > 0) {
2732:       const CHUNK_SIZE = 100;
2733:       // Max number of chunks to process to avoid unbounded DB round-trips.
2734:       // Configurable via env IMPACT_MAX_CHUNKS, default 10 => max items = 1000
2735:       const MAX_CHUNKS = parseInt(process.env.IMPACT_MAX_CHUNKS || '10', 10);
2736: 
2737:       // ── Process enrichment: batched chunking (bounded by MAX_CHUNKS) ─
2738:       // Uses merged Cypher query (WITH + OPTIONAL MATCH) to fetch
2739:       // process + entry point info in 1 round-trip per chunk. Converted to
2740:       // parameterized queries to avoid manual string escaping and long query strings.
2741:       const entryPointMap = new Map<
2742:         string,
2743:         {
2744:           name: string;
2745:           type: string;
2746:           filePath: string;
2747:           affected_process_count: number;
2748:           total_hits: number;
2749:           earliest_broken_step: number;
2750:         }
2751:       >();
2752: 
2753:       // Map process id -> entryPointId to allow fixing missing minStep values later
2754:       const processToEntryPoint = new Map<string, string>();
2755:       // Collect process ids where MIN(r.step) returned null so we can retry in batch
2756:       const processesMissingMinStep = new Set<string>();
2757: 
2758:       let chunksProcessed = 0;
2759:       for (
2760:         let i = 0;

2761:         i < impacted.length && chunksProcessed < MAX_CHUNKS;
2762:         i += CHUNK_SIZE, chunksProcessed++
2763:       ) {
2764:         const chunk = impacted.slice(i, i + CHUNK_SIZE);
2765:         const ids = chunk.map((item) => String(item.id ?? ''));
2766: 
2767:         try {
2768:           // Use parameterized list to avoid building long query strings
2769:           const rows = await executeParameterized(
2770:             repo.id,
2771:             `
2772:             MATCH (s)-[r:CodeRelation {type: 'STEP_IN_PROCESS'}]->(p:Process)
2773:             WHERE s.id IN $ids
2774:             WITH p, COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) AS hits, MIN(r.step) AS minStep
2775:             OPTIONAL MATCH (ep {id: p.entryPointId})
2776:             RETURN p.id AS pId, p.heuristicLabel AS name, p.processType AS processType,
2777:                    p.entryPointId AS entryPointId, hits, minStep, p.stepCount AS stepCount,
2778:                    ep.name AS epName, labels(ep)[0] AS epType, ep.filePath AS epFilePath
2779:           `,
2780:             { ids },
2781:           ).catch(() => []);
2782: 
2783:           for (const row of rows) {
2784:             const pId = row.pId ?? row[0];
2785:             const epId = row.entryPointId ?? row[3] ?? row.pId ?? row[0];
2786:             // Track mapping from process -> entryPoint so we can backfill missing minStep
2787:             if (pId) processToEntryPoint.set(String(pId), String(epId));
2788: 
2789:             // Normalize epName: prefer epName, fall back to other columns, and
2790:             // ensure we don't keep an empty string (labels(...) can return "").
2791:             const epNameRaw = row.epName ?? row[7] ?? row.name ?? row[1] ?? 'unknown';
2792:             const epName =
2793:               typeof epNameRaw === 'string' && epNameRaw.trim().length > 0
2794:                 ? epNameRaw.trim()
2795:                 : 'unknown';
2796: 
2797:             // Normalize epType: labels(ep)[0] can return an empty string in
2798:             // some DBs (LadybugDB). Using nullish coalescing (??) preserves
2799:             // empty strings, which results in empty `type` values being
2800:             // propagated. Treat empty-string labels as missing and fall back
2801:             // to the next candidate or a sensible default.
2802:             const epTypeRaw = row.epType ?? row[8] ?? '';
2803:             const epType =
2804:               typeof epTypeRaw === 'string' && epTypeRaw.trim().length > 0
2805:                 ? epTypeRaw.trim()
2806:                 : 'Function';
2807: 
2808:             const epFilePath = row.epFilePath ?? row[9] ?? '';
2809:             const hits = row.hits ?? row[4] ?? 0;
2810:             const minStep = row.minStep ?? row[5];
2811:             // If the DB returned null for minStep, note the process id so we
2812:             // can run a follow-up query using a different aggregation strategy.
2813:             if (minStep === null || minStep === undefined) {
2814:               if (pId) processesMissingMinStep.add(String(pId));
2815:             }
2816:             if (!entryPointMap.has(epId)) {
2817:               entryPointMap.set(epId, {
2818:                 name: epName,
2819:                 type: epType,
2820:                 filePath: epFilePath,
2821:                 affected_process_count: 0,
2822:                 total_hits: 0,
2823:                 earliest_broken_step: Infinity,
2824:               });
2825:             }
2826:             const ep = entryPointMap.get(epId)!;
2827:             ep.affected_process_count += 1;
2828:             ep.total_hits += hits;
2829:             ep.earliest_broken_step = Math.min(ep.earliest_broken_step, minStep ?? Infinity);
2830:           }
2831:         } catch (e) {
2832:           logQueryError('impact:process-chunk', e);
2833:         }
2834:       }
2835: 
2836:       // If some processes returned null minStep, try a batched follow-up query
2837:       // using the full impacted id set. This handles older indexes or DBs
2838:       // where MIN(r.step) can come back null even when step properties exist.
2839:       if (processesMissingMinStep.size > 0) {
2840:         try {
2841:           const pIds = Array.from(processesMissingMinStep);
2842:           const allImpactedIds = impacted.map((it) => String(it.id ?? ''));
2843:           const missingRows = await executeParameterized(
2844:             repo.id,
2845:             `
2846:             MATCH (s)-[r:CodeRelation {type: 'STEP_IN_PROCESS'}]->(p:Process)
2847:             WHERE p.id IN $pIds AND s.id IN $ids
2848:             RETURN p.id AS pid, MIN(r.step) AS minStep
2849:           `,
2850:             { pIds, ids: allImpactedIds },
2851:           ).catch(() => []);
2852: 
2853:           for (const mr of missingRows) {
2854:             const pid = mr.pid ?? mr[0];
2855:             const minStep = mr.minStep ?? mr[1];
2856:             const epId = processToEntryPoint.get(String(pid));
2857:             if (!epId) continue;
2858:             const ep = entryPointMap.get(epId);
2859:             if (!ep) continue;
2860:             if (typeof minStep === 'number') {
2861:               ep.earliest_broken_step = Math.min(ep.earliest_broken_step, minStep);
2862:             }
2863:           }
2864:         } catch (e) {
2865:           logQueryError('impact:process-chunk-backfill', e);
2866:         }
2867:       }
2868: 
2869:       // If we capped chunks, mark traversal incomplete so caller knows results are partial
2870:       if (chunksProcessed * CHUNK_SIZE < impacted.length) {
2871:         traversalComplete = false;
2872:       }
2873: 
2874:       affectedProcesses = Array.from(entryPointMap.values())
2875:         .map((ep) => ({
2876:           ...ep,
2877:           earliest_broken_step:
2878:             ep.earliest_broken_step === Infinity ? null : ep.earliest_broken_step,
2879:         }))
2880:         .sort((a, b) => b.total_hits - a.total_hits);
2881: 
2882:       // ── Module enrichment: use same cap as process enrichment and parameterized queries
2883:       const maxItems = Math.min(impacted.length, MAX_CHUNKS * CHUNK_SIZE);
2884:       const cappedImpacted = impacted.slice(0, maxItems);
2885:       const allIdsArr = cappedImpacted.map((i: any) => String(i.id ?? ''));
2886:       const d1Items = (grouped[1] || []).slice(0, maxItems);
2887:       const d1IdsArr = d1Items.map((i: any) => String(i.id ?? ''));
2888: 
2889:       // Chunked module enrichment: run the MEMBER_OF queries in chunks
2890:       // to avoid large single queries or concurrent Kuzu calls that can
2891:       // crash (SIGSEGV) on arm64 macOS; behavior preserves existing maxItems cap and returns equivalent aggregated results.
2892:       const moduleHitsMap = new Map<string, number>();
2893:       const directModuleSet = new Set<string>();
2894: 
2895:       // Helper to run a single module chunk and accumulate hits by name
2896:       const runModuleChunk = async (idsChunk: string[]) => {
2897:         if (!idsChunk || idsChunk.length === 0) return;
2898:         try {
2899:           const rows = await executeParameterized(
2900:             repo.id,
2901:             `
2902:             MATCH (s)-[:CodeRelation {type: 'MEMBER_OF'}]->(c:Community)
2903:             WHERE s.id IN $ids
2904:             RETURN c.heuristicLabel AS name, COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) AS hits
2905:             ORDER BY hits DESC
2906:             LIMIT 20
2907:           `,
2908:             { ids: idsChunk },
2909:           ).catch(() => []);
2910: 
2911:           for (const r of rows) {
2912:             const name = r.name ?? r[0] ?? null;
2913:             const hits = (r.hits ?? r[1]) || 0;
2914:             if (!name) continue;
2915:             moduleHitsMap.set(name, (moduleHitsMap.get(name) || 0) + hits);
2916:           }
2917:         } catch (e) {
2918:           logQueryError('impact:module-chunk', e);
2919:         }
2920:       };
2921: 
2922:       // Run module query chunks sequentially (safe on arm64 macOS)
2923:       for (let i = 0; i < allIdsArr.length; i += CHUNK_SIZE) {
2924:         const chunkIds = allIdsArr.slice(i, i + CHUNK_SIZE);

 454:     // avoid an fs.readFile round-trip on every tool invocation.
 455:     if (this.initializedRepos.has(repoId) && isLbugReady(repoId)) {

FILE: Z:/repos/deps/gitnexus/docs/code-indexing/cobol/README.md
   1: # COBOL Code Indexing
   2: 
   3: GitNexus indexes COBOL codebases using a **regex-only extraction** strategy, bypassing tree-sitter entirely. This document explains why, how the pipeline works, and links to detailed sub-documents.
   4: 
   5: ## Why Regex-Only?
   6: 
   7: The tree-sitter-cobol grammar (v0.0.1) has three critical limitations that make it unusable for production indexing:
   8: 
   9: | Issue | Impact | Severity |
  10: |-------|--------|----------|
  11: | External scanner hangs on ~5% of files | No timeout mechanism exists for the C scanner; the process blocks indefinitely | **Blocking** |
  12: | Only ~15% of paragraph headers detected | Most procedure-division paragraphs are invisible to the grammar | High |
  13: | Patch markers in cols 1-6 cause parse errors | Enterprise COBOL uses non-standard sequence area content (e.g., `mzADD`, `estero`, `#FIX`) | High |
  14: 
  15: Because the external scanner hang cannot be interrupted (there is no `setTimeoutMicros` equivalent for tree-sitter), using tree-sitter-cobol would hang the indexing pipeline on a non-trivial fraction of real-world files.
  16: 
  17: The regex-only approach provides:
  18: 
  19: - **Speed**: ~1ms per file average extraction time
  20: - **Reliability**: zero hangs, zero crashes across 13,000+ files
  21: - **Coverage**: captures all critical symbols -- program name, paragraphs, sections, CALL, PERFORM, COPY, data items (01-77, 88-level), file declarations, FD entries, EXEC SQL/CICS blocks, ENTRY points, and MOVE statements
  22: 
  23: ## Architecture
  24: 
  25: ```mermaid
  26: flowchart TD
  27:     A[Repository Scan] --> B{File Detection}
  28:     B -->|Extension match| C[COBOL file]
  29:     B -->|GITNEXUS_COBOL_DIRS match| C
  30:     B -->|No match| Z[Skip]
  31: 
  32:     C --> D{Copybook?}
  33:     D -->|Yes| E[Add to Copybook Map]
  34:     D -->|No| F[Source Program]
  35: 
  36:     E --> G[COPY Expansion Engine]
  37:     F --> G
  38: 
  39:     G -->|Inline copybook content| H[Expanded Source]
  40:     H --> I[Patch Marker Cleanup]
  41:     I --> J[Regex State Machine]
  42: 
  43:     J --> K[Extracted Symbols]
  44:     K --> L[Graph Model Builder]
  45:     L --> M[Knowledge Graph]
  46: 
  47:     subgraph "Per-Chunk Processing"
  48:         G
  49:         H
  50:         I
  51:         J
  52:         K
  53:         L
  54:     end
  55: 
  56:     subgraph "Post-Processing"
  57:         M --> N[Community Detection]
  58:         M --> O[Process Detection]
  59:         M --> P[Contract Detection]
  60:     end
  61: 
  62:     style J fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32
  63:     style G fill:#e3f2fd,stroke:#1565c0
  64: ```
  65: 
  66: ## COBOL vs Tree-Sitter Languages
  67: 
  68: | Feature | COBOL (Regex) | Tree-Sitter Languages |
  69: |---------|--------------|----------------------|
  70: | Parser | Single-pass regex state machine | tree-sitter grammar + queries |
  71: | Speed | ~1ms/file | ~5ms/file |
  72: | AST available | No | Yes |
  73: | COPY expansion | Yes (pre-processing step) | N/A |
  74: | Deep indexing | Data items, SQL, CICS, FD, ENTRY | Type annotations, generics, etc. |
  75: | Call extraction | PERFORM (intra-file) + CALL (cross-program) | AST-based call site detection |
  76: | Import extraction | COPY statements | `import`/`require`/`use`/`#include` |
  77: | Coverage | All critical symbols | Language-dependent query coverage |
  78: | Failure mode | Never hangs | External scanner can hang (COBOL only) |
  79:

   1: # COBOL File Detection
   2: 
   3: GitNexus detects COBOL files through two mechanisms: extension-based mapping and directory-based override for extensionless files. This document covers both, plus the copybook/program classification logic.
   4: 
   5: ## Extension Mapping
   6: 
   7: ### Program Extensions
   8: 
   9: | Extension | Type |
  10: |-----------|------|
  11: | `.cbl` | COBOL program |
  12: | `.cob` | COBOL program |
  13: | `.cobol` | COBOL program |
  14: 
  15: ### Copybook Extensions
  16: 
  17: | Extension | Type | Notes |
  18: |-----------|------|-------|
  19: | `.cpy` | Copybook | Standard |
  20: | `.copy` | Copybook | Standard |
  21: | `.gnm` / `.GNM` | Copybook | Enterprise (GnuCOBOL naming) |
  22: | `.fd` / `.FD` | Copybook | File Description fragment |
  23: | `.wrk` / `.WRK` | Copybook | Working-Storage fragment |
  24: | `.sel` / `.SEL` | Copybook | SELECT clause fragment |
  25: | `.open` / `.OPEN` | Copybook | File OPEN fragment |
  26: | `.close` / `.CLOSE` | Copybook | File CLOSE fragment |
  27: | `.ini` / `.INI` | Copybook | Initialization fragment |
  28: | `.def` / `.DEF` | Copybook | Definition fragment |
  29: 
  30: All extension matching is case-sensitive in `getLanguageFromFilename` (the extensions above are matched as written, including uppercase variants like `.GNM`).
  31: 
  32: ## Extensionless File Detection: `GITNEXUS_COBOL_DIRS`
  33: 
  34: Many enterprise COBOL repositories use extensionless files -- the filename alone identifies the program (e.g., `s/BGTABFL` is the source for program `BGTABFL`). GitNexus handles this via the `GITNEXUS_COBOL_DIRS` environment variable.
  35: 
  36: ### Configuration
  37: 
  38: Set `GITNEXUS_COBOL_DIRS` to a comma-separated list of directory names:
  39: 
  40: ```bash
  41: # Files in s/, c/, and wfproc/ directories (at any depth) are treated as COBOL
  42: export GITNEXUS_COBOL_DIRS=s,c,wfproc
  43: ```
  44: 
  45: The matching is **case-insensitive** and checks all path segments:
  46: 
  47: - `/repo/s/BGTABFL` -- matches segment `s` -- COBOL
  48: - `/repo/src/c/CPSESP` -- matches segment `c` -- COBOL
  49: - `/repo/wfproc/WF001` -- matches segment `wfproc` -- COBOL
  50: - `/repo/docs/README` -- no matching segment -- skipped
  51: 
  52: ### Decision Tree
  53: 
  54: ```mermaid
  55: flowchart TD
  56:     A[getLanguageFromPath] --> B[getLanguageFromFilename]
  57:     B --> C{Known extension?}
  58:     C -->|Yes .cbl/.cob/.cobol/.cpy/...| D[Return COBOL]
  59:     C -->|Yes .ts/.py/.java/...| E[Return other language]
  60:     C -->|No match| F{Has extension?}
  61: 
  62:     F -->|"Has dot in basename"| G[Return null]
  63:     F -->|"No dot = extensionless"| H{GITNEXUS_COBOL_DIRS set?}
  64: 
  65:     H -->|No| G
  66:     H -->|Yes| I{Any path segment<br/>matches a configured dir?}
  67: 
  68:     I -->|Yes| D
  69:     I -->|No| G
  70: 
  71:     style D fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32
  72:     style G fill:#ffebee,stroke:#c62828
  73: ```
  74: 
  75: ### Implementation Detail
  76: 
  77: The `GITNEXUS_COBOL_DIRS` value is parsed once (on first call) and cached in a `Set<string>`:
  78: 
  79: ```typescript
  80: // From gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/utils.ts
  81: const getCobolDirs = (): Set<string> => {
  82:   if (_cobolDirs) return _cobolDirs;
  83:   const raw = process.env.GITNEXUS_COBOL_DIRS;
  84:   _cobolDirs = raw
  85:     ? new Set(raw.split(',').map(d => d.trim().toLowerCase()))
  86:     : new Set();
  87:   return _cobolDirs;
  88: };
  89: ```
  90: 
  91: The path segment check splits the full path on `/` and tests each segment against the cached set.
  92: 
  93: ## Copybook vs Program Classification
  94: 
  95: After a file is identified as COBOL, it must be classified as either a **program** (to be parsed for symbols) or a **copybook** (to be loaded into the copybook map for COPY expansion).
  96: 
  97: ### Classification Rules
  98: 
  99: A COBOL file is classified as a **copybook** if ANY of these conditions is true:
 100: 
 101: 1. It has a recognized copybook extension (`.cpy`, `.copy`, `.gnm`, `.fd`, `.wrk`, `.sel`, `.open`, `.close`, `.ini`, `.def`)
 102: 2. It is an extensionless file whose path contains a directory segment matching one of: `c`, `copy`, `copybooks`, `copylib`, `cpy`
 103: 
 104: A file is classified as a **program** if:
 105: 
 106: 1. It has a program extension (`.cbl`, `.cob`, `.cobol`), OR
 107: 2. It is extensionless and does NOT match any copybook directory pattern
 108: 
 109: ### Copybook Name Resolution
 110: 
 111: Copybook names are derived from the filename:
 112: 
 113: - Strip the extension (if any)
 114: - Convert to uppercase
 115: 
 116: Examples:
 117: - `c/CPSESP` -- name: `CPSESP`
 118: - `copy/workgrid.cpy` -- name: `WORKGRID`
 119: - `c/ANAZI.GNM` -- name: `ANAZI`
 120: 
 121: This name is used to resolve `COPY CPSESP.` statements during expansion.
 122: 
 123: ## Source Files
 124: 
 125: - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/utils.ts` -- `getLanguageFromPath()`, `getLanguageFromFilename()`, `getCobolDirs()`
 126: - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/pipeline.ts` -- `isCobolCopybook()`, `getCopybookName()`, `COPYBOOK_EXTENSIONS`, `COBOL_PROGRAM_EXTENSIONS`
FILE: Z:/repos/deps/gitnexus/docs/code-indexing/cobol/copy-expansion.md
   1: # COBOL COPY Expansion
   2: 
   3: The COPY statement is COBOL's include mechanism -- analogous to `#include` in C or `import` in modern languages. GitNexus expands COPY statements **before** regex extraction so that symbols defined inside copybooks (data items, paragraphs, etc.) are visible in the program's extracted graph.
   4: 
   5: ## Supported Syntax
   6: 
   7: ### Basic COPY
   8: 
   9: ```cobol
  10: COPY CPSESP.
  11: COPY "WORKGRID.CPY".
  12: ```
  13: 
  14: Inlines the content of the named copybook, replacing the COPY line(s).
  15: 
  16: ### COPY with REPLACING
  17: 
  18: ```cobol
  19: COPY CPSESP REPLACING "ANAZI-KEY" BY "LK-KEY".
  20: COPY CPSESP REPLACING LEADING "ESP-" BY "LK-ESP-"
  21:                        LEADING "KPSESPL" BY "LK-KPSESPL".
  22: COPY LINKAGE REPLACING TRAILING "-IN" BY "-OUT".
  23: ```
  24: 
  25: Three REPLACING types are supported:
  26: 
  27: | Type         | Syntax                               | Behavior                                | Example                          |
  28: | ------------ | ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
  29: | **EXACT**    | `REPLACING "OLD" BY "NEW"`           | Replace exact identifier matches        | `ANAZI-KEY` becomes `LK-KEY`     |
  30: | **LEADING**  | `REPLACING LEADING "PFX-" BY "NEW-"` | Replace prefix on all COBOL identifiers | `ESP-NAME` becomes `LK-ESP-NAME` |
  31: | **TRAILING** | `REPLACING TRAILING "-IN" BY "-OUT"` | Replace suffix on all COBOL identifiers | `DATA-IN` becomes `DATA-OUT`     |
  32: 
  33: Multiple REPLACING clauses can appear in a single COPY statement. They are applied in order to each COBOL identifier in the copybook content.
  34: 
  35: ### Multi-Line COPY
  36: 
  37: COPY statements can span multiple lines (standard COBOL continuation rules apply):
  38: 
  39: ```cobol
  40:        COPY CPSESP REPLACING
  41:       -    LEADING "ESP-" BY "LK-ESP-"
  42:       -    LEADING "KPSESPL" BY "LK-KPSESPL".
  43: ```
  44: 
  45: Continuation lines (indicator `-` in column 7) are merged before COPY statement scanning.
  46: 
  47: ## Expansion Flow
  48: 
  49: ```mermaid
  50: sequenceDiagram
  51:     participant Pipeline
  52:     participant Expander as COPY Expander
  53:     participant Resolver
  54:     participant Reader
  55: 
  56:     Pipeline->>Pipeline: Identify all COBOL files
  57:     Pipeline->>Pipeline: Classify copybooks vs programs
  58:     Pipeline->>Reader: Read all copybook content upfront
  59:     Reader-->>Pipeline: Copybook content map (name -> content)
  60: 
  61:     loop For each source file in chunk
  62:         Pipeline->>Expander: expandCopies(content, filePath, resolveFile, readFile)
  63:         Expander->>Expander: Merge continuation lines
  64:         Expander->>Expander: Detect COPY statements via regex
  65: 
  66:         loop For each COPY statement (reverse order)
  67:             Expander->>Resolver: resolveFile(copyTarget)
  68:             Resolver-->>Expander: Copybook key or null
  69: 
  70:             alt Resolved successfully
  71:                 Expander->>Reader: readFile(resolvedKey)
  72:                 Reader-->>Expander: Copybook content
  73: 
  74:                 Expander->>Expander: Apply REPLACING transformations
  75:                 Expander->>Expander: Recurse for nested COPYs (depth + 1)
  76:                 Expander->>Expander: Splice expanded content into output
  77:             else Not resolved
  78:                 Expander->>Expander: Keep original COPY line
  79:             end
  80:         end
  81: 
  82:         Expander-->>Pipeline: Expanded content + resolution metadata
  83:         Pipeline->>Pipeline: Replace file content with expanded content
  84:     end
  85: ```
  86: 
  87: The return type `CopyExpansionResult` contains `expandedContent` and `copyResolutions`. The `expansionDepth` field has been removed from the return type (it was unused by callers).
  88: 
  89: COPY statement line numbers in `CopyResolution` are 1-based (consistent with the preprocessor's line numbering). The splice operation that replaces COPY lines with expanded content adjusts for 0-based array indexing internally.
  90: 
  91: ## Cycle Detection
  92: 
  93: Circular COPY references (e.g., copybook A includes copybook B which includes copybook A) are detected and handled:
  94: 
  95: 1. Each expansion chain maintains a `visited` set of resolved copybook paths
  96: 2. If a copybook path is already in the visited set, the expansion is skipped
  97: 3. A `warnedCircular` set (internal to `expandCopies()`, not a parameter) deduplicates warning messages within a single file expansion
  98: 
  99: Known circular copybooks in PROJECT-NAME: `ANAZI`, `ANDIP`, `QDIPE` (self-referential includes).
 100: 
 101: ## Max Depth
 102: 
 103: Nested COPY expansion is limited to **10 levels** (`DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH`). If a COPY chain exceeds this depth, a warning is logged and the remaining COPY statements are left unexpanded.
 104: 
 105: ## Max Total Expansions
 106: 
 107: A breadth amplification guard caps the total number of COPY expansions across all branches within a single file to **500** (`MAX_TOTAL_EXPANSIONS`). This prevents exponential blowup from diamond-shaped COPY graphs where N copybooks each include N other copybooks. Once the limit is reached, further COPY statements in that file are left unexpanded and a single warning is logged.
 108: 
 109: ## REPLACING Application Detail
 110: 
 111: The REPLACING engine works by scanning all COBOL identifiers (matching `\b[A-Z][A-Z0-9-]*\b`) in the copybook content and applying each replacement rule:
 112: 
 113: ```
 114: Original copybook content:
 115:        05  ESP-NAME          PIC X(30).
 116:        05  ESP-CODE          PIC X(10).
 117:        05  KPSESPL-FLAG      PIC X(01).
 118: 
 119: After REPLACING LEADING "ESP-" BY "LK-ESP-" LEADING "KPSESPL" BY "LK-KPSESPL":
 120:        05  LK-ESP-NAME       PIC X(30).
 121:        05  LK-ESP-CODE       PIC X(10).
 122:        05  LK-KPSESPL-FLAG   PIC X(01).
 123: ```
 124: 
 125: For LEADING replacements, the engine checks if each identifier starts with the `from` prefix (case-insensitive) and replaces only the prefix portion, preserving the rest of the identifier.
 126: 
 127: For TRAILING replacements, the same logic applies to suffixes.
 128: 
 129: For EXACT replacements, only identifiers that match the `from` value exactly (case-insensitive) are replaced.
 130: 
 131: ## Copybook Resolution
 132: 
 133: The resolver tries multiple strategies to match a COPY target name to a copybook file:
 134: 
 135: 1. **Exact match**: `COPY CPSESP` resolves to copybook named `CPSESP`
 136: 2. **Strip extension**: `COPY WORKGRID.CPY` strips `.CPY` and resolves to `WORKGRID`
 137: 3. **Add extension**: `COPY CPSESP` tries `CPSESP.CPY` and `CPSESP.COPY`
 138: 
 139: If no match is found, the COPY statement is left in place (unexpanded) and a resolution record with `resolvedPath: null` is created.
 140: 
 141: ## Pipeline Integration
 142: 
 143: The expansion runs **per chunk**, after file content is read but before dispatch to worker threads:
 144: 
 145: 1. All copybook files are read upfront (they are typically small, collectively under 100MB)
 146: 2. Per chunk, the copybook map is merged with chunk content (in case a chunk contains copybooks)
 147: 3. Only programs (not copybooks themselves) undergo expansion
 148: 4. The expanded content replaces the original content in-place before worker dispatch
 149: 
 150: ## Inline Comment Handling
 151: 
 152: The copy expander's `stripInlineComment()` helper is quote-aware: pipe characters (`|`) inside single- or double-quoted strings are preserved. This matches the same quote-aware logic used by the preprocessor.
 153: 
 154: ## Source Files
 155: 
 156: - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/cobol-copy-expander.ts` -- `expandCopies()`, `parseReplacingClause()`, `applyReplacing()`
 157: - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/pipeline.ts` -- `expandCobolCopies()`, copybook map construction, chunk integration

   1: # COBOL Performance and Tuning
   2: 
   3: This document covers real-world benchmarks, worker pool configuration, memory management, known limitations, and troubleshooting for COBOL indexing.
   4: 
   5: ## PROJECT-NAME Benchmark
   6: 
   7: The PROJECT-NAME project is a large Italian payroll system written in COBOL. It serves as the primary benchmark for COBOL indexing performance.
   8: 
   9: ### Input
  10: 
  11: | Metric                      | Value                                                                        |
  12: | --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

  73: ## Worker Pool Tuning
  74: 
  75: ### Sub-Batch Size
  76: 
  77: The worker pool splits each worker's chunk into sub-batches to bound peak memory per `postMessage` serialization. COBOL repos use a smaller sub-batch size than the default:
  78: 
  79: | Parameter             | Default     | COBOL Mode          |
  80: | --------------------- | ----------- | ------------------- |
  81: | Sub-batch size        | 1,500 files | 200 files           |
  82: | Per sub-batch timeout | 120s        | 120s (configurable) |
  83: 
  84: **Why 200?** COBOL regex extraction + preprocessing takes ~1ms per file on average, but with COPY expansion and deep indexing the effective time is ~150ms per file. At sub-batch size 1500, that would be ~225s per sub-batch, exceeding the 120s timeout.
  85: 
  86: COBOL mode is activated automatically when `GITNEXUS_COBOL_DIRS` is set:
  87: 
  88: ```typescript
  89: // From pipeline.ts
  90: const cobolSubBatch = process.env.GITNEXUS_COBOL_DIRS ? 200 : undefined;
  91: workerPool = createWorkerPool(workerUrl, undefined, cobolSubBatch);
  92: ```
  93: 
  94: ### Worker Count
  95: 
  96: Workers default to `min(8, cpus - 1)`. For COBOL repos, this is usually sufficient since regex extraction is CPU-bound but fast. The bottleneck is typically KuzuDB write, not extraction.
  97: 
  98: ### Timeout Configuration
  99: 
 100: | Environment Variable                 | Default         | Purpose                                             |
 101: | ------------------------------------ | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
 102: | `GITNEXUS_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS`         | 120,000 (2 min) | Per sub-batch processing timeout                    |
 103: | `GITNEXUS_WORKER_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS` | 60,000 (1 min)  | Worker initialization timeout (tree-sitter loading) |
 104: 
 105: For COBOL-only repos, worker startup is faster because tree-sitter native modules are loaded lazily (skipped entirely if only COBOL files are present).
 106: 
 107: ## Data Item Cap
 108: 
 109: ### Configuration
 110: 
 111: ```typescript
 112: const MAX_DATA_ITEMS_PER_FILE = 500;
 113: ```
 114: 
 115: This constant appears in both `parse-worker.ts` (worker path) and `parsing-processor.ts` (sequential fallback).
 116: 
 117: ### Rationale
 118: 
 119: Some COBOL programs, especially after COPY expansion, can have 10,000+ data items. At that scale:
 120: 
 121: - The in-memory relationship Map (for CONTAINS, REDEFINES, etc.) approaches the V8 16.7M entry limit across thousands of files
 122: - KuzuDB write time increases linearly with edge count
 123: - Most deep-nested items (level 20+) are rarely queried individually
 124: 
 125: ### Impact
 126: 
 127: The cap truncates data items beyond the 500th in source order. Since 01-level Records appear first in COBOL source, the cap preserves:
 128: 
 129: - All 01-level record definitions
 130: - The most important 02-49 level items (those closest to the record root)
 131: - 88-level conditions associated with early items
 132: 
 133: To increase the cap for specific needs, modify the `MAX_DATA_ITEMS_PER_FILE` constant in both files.
 134: 
 135: ## Memory Management
 136: 
 137: ### COPY Expansion Breadth Guard
 138: 
 139: A per-file `MAX_TOTAL_EXPANSIONS = 500` limit prevents exponential blowup from diamond-shaped COPY graphs (e.g., N copybooks each containing N COPY statements). Once the limit is reached, further COPY statements in that file are left unexpanded. See [copy-expansion.md](copy-expansion.md) for details.
 140: 
 141: ### COPY Expansion Memory
 142: 
 143: All copybook content is loaded upfront into a Map before chunk processing begins. For PROJECT-NAME:
 144: 
 145: - 2,976 copybooks, typically under 100MB total
 146: - The Map is shared (read-only) across chunk iterations
 147: - Per-chunk, the copybook map is merged with chunk file content (in case a chunk contains copybooks not in the pre-loaded set)
 148: - After all chunks are processed, the copybook map is freed (`cobolCopybookContents = undefined`)
 149: 
 150: ### Chunk Budget
 151: 
 152: Source files are grouped into chunks of max 20MB (`CHUNK_BYTE_BUDGET`). Each chunk's lifecycle:
 153: 
 154: 1. Read file content into memory
 155: 2. Expand COPY statements (mutates content in-place)
 156: 3. Dispatch to workers for extraction
 157: 4. Workers return serialized results
 158: 5. Merge results into graph
 159: 6. Chunk content goes out of scope (GC reclaims)
 160: 
 161: This ensures only ~20MB of source + ~200-400MB of working memory (ASTs, extracted records, serialization) is active at any time.
 162: 
 163: ### Shared Warning Deduplication
 164: 
 165: The `warnedCircular` set (used by the COPY expansion engine) is shared across all files in a chunk. This prevents the same circular copybook warning (e.g., `ANAZI includes itself`) from being logged thousands of times.
 166: 
 167: ## Known Limitations
 168: 
 169: | Limitation                               | Impact                                                                                                          | Workaround                                                 |
 170: | ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
 171: | tree-sitter-cobol hangs on ~5% of files  | Cannot use tree-sitter for COBOL                                                                                | Regex-only extraction (current approach)                   |
 172: | Data item cap (500/file)                 | May miss deeply nested items in large programs                                                                  | Increase `MAX_DATA_ITEMS_PER_FILE` in source               |
 173: | Circular copybooks (ANAZI, ANDIP, QDIPE) | Self-referential includes cannot be expanded                                                                    | Detected and skipped with warning                          |
 174: | wfproc/ files may not be pure COBOL      | Workflow files may produce extraction noise                                                                     | Exclude `wfproc` from `GITNEXUS_COBOL_DIRS` if problematic |
 175: | No MOVE DATA_FLOW edges yet              | Data flow between variables not in graph                                                                        | Reserved for future release                                |
 176: | Continuation line handling               | Some complex multi-line continuations (especially in string literals spanning 3+ lines) may not merge correctly | Known edge case; affects <0.1% of lines                    |
 177: | Single-line EXEC blocks                  | `EXEC SQL SELECT ... END-EXEC` on one line is handled, but pathological nesting is not                          | Extremely rare in practice                                 |
 178: | Extension case sensitivity               | `.GNM` and `.gnm` are matched differently                                                                       | Use the exact case from the codebase                       |
 179: 
 180: ## Troubleshooting
 181: 
 182: ### "COPY expansion failed"
 183: 
 184: ```
 185: [pipeline] COPY expansion failed for s/BGTABFL: Cannot read properties of null
 186: ```
 187: 
 188: **Cause:** A copybook referenced by a COPY statement cannot be found.
 189: 
 190: **Fix:**
 191: 
 192: 1. Verify `GITNEXUS_COBOL_DIRS` includes the directory containing copybooks (typically `c`)
 193: 2. Check that copybook filenames match the COPY target (case-insensitive, after stripping extensions)
 194: 3. Ensure copybook files are not in `.gitignore`
 195: 
 196: ### Worker sub-batch timeout
 197: 
 198: ```
 199: Worker 3 sub-batch timed out after 120s (chunk: 200 items)
 200: ```
 201: 
 202: **Cause:** A sub-batch took longer than the timeout. Typically happens when one file is extremely large (50,000+ lines after COPY expansion).
 203: 
 204: **Fix:** Increase the timeout:
 205: 
 206: ```bash
 207: GITNEXUS_WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS=300000 gitnexus analyze
 208: ```
 209: 
 210: ### Memory errors (heap out of memory)
 211: 
 212: ```
 213: FATAL ERROR: CALL_AND_RETRY_LAST Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
 214: ```
 215: 
 216: **Fix:** Increase Node.js heap size:
 217: 
 218: ```bash
 219: node --max-old-space-size=16384 /path/to/gitnexus/dist/cli/index.js analyze
 220: ```
 221: 
 222: For very large repos (>500MB source), consider `--max-old-space-size=32768`.
 223: 
 224: ### Concurrent analyze corruption
 225: 
 226: **Rule:** Only ONE `gitnexus analyze` process should run at a time per repository. Concurrent writes to KuzuDB corrupt the database.
 227: 
 228: If corruption occurs:
 229: 
 230: ```bash
 231: # Remove the KuzuDB directory and re-index
 232: rm -rf .gitnexus/kuzu
 233: gitnexus analyze --force
 234: ```
 235: 
 236: ### Slow KuzuDB write phase
 237: 
 238: The KuzuDB write phase (132s for PROJECT-NAME) is the bottleneck for large COBOL repos. This is proportional to the number of nodes and edges being written. Reducing `MAX_DATA_ITEMS_PER_FILE` or excluding non-essential directories from `GITNEXUS_COBOL_DIRS` can help.
 239: 
 240: ### Verbose output
 241: 
 242: Enable verbose logging to see per-phase timing and statistics:
 243: 
 244: ```bash
 245: GITNEXUS_VERBOSE=1 gitnexus analyze
 246: ```
 247: 
 248: This outputs:
 249: 
 250: - Scan statistics (paths, parseable files, chunk count)
 251: - Worker pool configuration (worker count, sub-batch size)
 252: - COPY expansion statistics (copybooks loaded, files expanded)
 253: - Community and process detection results
 254: - Contract detection results
 255: 
 256: ## Source Files
 257: 
 258: - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/workers/worker-pool.ts` -- `DEFAULT_SUB_BATCH_SIZE`, `SUB_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS`, `WORKER_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS`
 259: - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/pipeline.ts` -- `CHUNK_BYTE_BUDGET`, COBOL sub-batch configuration, chunk lifecycle
 260: - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/workers/parse-worker.ts` -- `MAX_DATA_ITEMS_PER_FILE`, `processCobolRegexOnly()`
 261: - `gitnexus/src/core/ingestion/parsing-processor.ts` -- Sequential fallback `MAX_DATA_ITEMS_PER_FILE`

   1: # Using GitNexus across Apache Thrift microservices
   2: 
   3: ## When to use this guide
   4: 
   5: Use this guide when several repositories communicate through Apache Thrift and you want GitNexus to trace impact across provider and consumer boundaries. The walkthrough assumes each service is indexed on its own, then joined through a GitNexus group.
   6: 
   7: This is not a framework integration guide. GitNexus reads portable Thrift IDL and common Java generated-code shapes. Framework-specific wiring, service discovery, deployment metadata, and private annotations belong outside the open-source core.
   8: 
   9: ## Mental model
  10: 
  11: - `.thrift` files define the canonical service contract. A method in an IDL service becomes a stable contract id in the form `thrift::<namespace>.<Service>/<Method>`.
  12: - Service wildcard ids in the form `thrift::<namespace>.<Service>/*` are supported as manifest and matching fallback forms when a service-level link is needed.
  13: - Java generated-code usage points GitNexus toward implementation and call sites. Providers commonly implement generated `Service.Iface`; consumers commonly hold or construct generated service interfaces or clients.
  14: - Group sync matches provider and consumer contracts with the same id, then cross-repo impact can hop through those links.
  15: - Framework-specific wiring should be modeled by extractor plugins, manifest links, or downstream integrations rather than hard-coded into core Thrift support.
  16: 
  17: ## Fictional IDL
  18: 
  19: ```thrift
  20: namespace java billing.v1
  21: 
  22: struct PlaceOrderRequest {
  23:   1: string orderId
  24:   2: double amount
  25: }
  26: 
  27: struct PlaceOrderResponse {
  28:   1: bool accepted
  29: }
  30: 
  31: struct GetOrderRequest {
  32:   1: string orderId
  33: }
  34: 
  35: struct GetOrderResponse {
  36:   1: string orderId
  37:   2: string status
  38: }
  39: 
  40: service OrderService {
  41:   PlaceOrderResponse PlaceOrder(1: PlaceOrderRequest request)
  42:   GetOrderResponse GetOrder(1: GetOrderRequest request)
  43: }
  44: ```
  45: 
  46: The service methods above produce canonical ids:
  47: 
  48: - `thrift::billing.v1.OrderService/PlaceOrder`
  49: - `thrift::billing.v1.OrderService/GetOrder`
  50: - `thrift::billing.v1.OrderService/*` as a service-level manifest or matching fallback form
  51: 
  52: ## Java provider example
  53: 
  54: Generated Java code usually exposes an `Iface` interface for the service. A provider implementation can be detected when it implements that generated interface.
  55: 
  56: ```java
  57: package example.billing;
  58: 
  59: import billing.v1.GetOrderRequest;
  60: import billing.v1.GetOrderResponse;
  61: import billing.v1.OrderService;
  62: import billing.v1.PlaceOrderRequest;
  63: import billing.v1.PlaceOrderResponse;
  64: 
  65: public final class OrderServiceHandler implements OrderService.Iface {
  66:   @Override
  67:   public PlaceOrderResponse PlaceOrder(PlaceOrderRequest request) {
  68:     return new PlaceOrderResponse(true);
  69:   }
  70: 
  71:   @Override
  72:   public GetOrderResponse GetOrder(GetOrderRequest request) {
  73:     return new GetOrderResponse(request.getOrderId(), "CREATED");
  74:   }
  75: }
  76: ```
  77: 
  78: With the IDL available, GitNexus can connect the implementation to `thrift::billing.v1.OrderService/PlaceOrder` and `thrift::billing.v1.OrderService/GetOrder`.
  79: 
  80: ## Java consumer examples
  81: 
  82: Consumers are strongest when Java usage can be tied back to the IDL namespace and service.
  83: 
  84: ```java
  85: package example.checkout;
  86: 
  87: import billing.v1.OrderService;
  88: import billing.v1.PlaceOrderRequest;
  89: 
  90: public final class CheckoutWorkflow {
  91:   private final OrderService.Iface orders;
  92: 
  93:   public CheckoutWorkflow(OrderService.Iface orders) {
  94:     this.orders = orders;
  95:   }
  96: 
  97:   public void submit(String orderId) throws Exception {
  98:     orders.PlaceOrder(new PlaceOrderRequest(orderId, 42.0));
  99:   }
 100: }
 101: ```
 102: 
 103: Some generated-code styles use the generated service type directly while keeping enough IDL context through imports and method calls.
 104: 
 105: ```java
 106: package example.reporting;
 107: 
 108: import billing.v1.GetOrderRequest;
 109: import billing.v1.OrderService;
 110: 
 111: public final class OrderLookup {
 112:   private final OrderService.Client client;
 113: 
 114:   public OrderLookup(OrderService.Client client) {
 115:     this.client = client;
 116:   }
 117: 
 118:   public String status(String orderId) throws Exception {
 119:     return client.GetOrder(new GetOrderRequest(orderId)).getStatus();
 120:   }
 121: }
 122: ```
 123: 
 124: When IDL context is missing, GitNexus may still emit a weaker consumer signal for generated `Iface` or `Client` shapes, but confidence is lower.
 125: 
 126: ## Group configuration
 127: 
 128: New group configs enable Thrift contract detection by default. Keep `detect.thrift: true`
 129: when a group should scan for Thrift contracts, or set it to `false` to skip Thrift
 130: extraction for that group.
 131: 
 132: ```yaml
 133: version: 1
 134: name: billing-platform
 135: description: Fictional services connected by Apache Thrift
 136: 
 137: repos:
 138:   checkout: checkout-service
 139:   billing: billing-service
 140: 
 141: links: []
 142: 
 143: detect:
 144:   http: true
 145:   grpc: false
 146:   thrift: true
 147:   topics: false
 148:   shared_libs: true
 149: ```
 150: 
 151: To disable Thrift extraction explicitly:
 152: 
 153: ```yaml
 154: detect:
 155:   thrift: false
 156: ```
 157: 
 158: After indexing each member repository, run group sync to extract contracts and write cross-repo links:
 159: 
 160: ```bash
 161: npx gitnexus group sync billing-platform
 162: ```
 163: 
 164: ## Manifest escape hatch
 165: 
 166: Use manifest links when automatic extraction cannot see a provider or consumer, or when generated code is wrapped behind an abstraction. Write the contract without the `thrift::` prefix; GitNexus canonicalizes it to the full Thrift contract id.
 167: 
 168: ```yaml
 169: links:
 170:   - from: checkout
 171:     to: billing
 172:     type: thrift
 173:     contract: billing.v1.OrderService/PlaceOrder
 174:     role: consumer
 175: ```
 176: 
 177: GitNexus canonicalizes that manifest entry to `thrift::billing.v1.OrderService/PlaceOrder` and uses it to connect the two repositories.
 178: 
 179: ## Known limitations
 180: 
 181: - Java detection currently targets v1 generated-code patterns.
 182: - Maven and POM dependency coordinates are not used for inference.
 183: - Framework-specific annotations and service discovery metadata are ignored by open-source Thrift extraction.
 184: - Ambiguous same-name services are skipped instead of guessed.
 185: - Java consumers without IDL context are lower confidence and limited to generated `Iface` and `Client` shapes.
